W: This picture of Chand Baori is stunning! I can’t
wait to go this summer.
M: It’s even more amazing in person. (A)Is it okay if
I tell you something about Indian culture?
W: Of course.
M: Well, feet are thought to be the dirtiest part of
the body in India, so it’s considered disrespectful
to touch books with your feet.
W: Disrespectful to books?
M: Yes, because books represent knowledge to
Indians. Touching them with your feet is like
touching another person with your feet.
W: But what if I accidentally touch a book with my
feet?
M: In that case, you should hold the book and
touch it to your forehead as a sign of apology.
W: Thanks for the information!
M: No problem! I hope you have a wonderful time
in India!

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: Can I tell you something about Indian culture?
May I tell you something about Indian culture?
Would you mind if I tell you something aboutIndian culture?
Is it all right if I tell you something aboutIndian culture?
Would you let me tell you something aboutIndian culture?
solution: ‘Would you mind if ~?’는 ‘제가 ~해도 괜찮을까요?’라는 의미 로 ‘Is if okay if ~?’와 같이 정중하게 허락을 구하는 표현으로 쓰이지만, 직역하면 ‘제가 ~한다면 싫으실까요?’라는 뜻으로, 수락할 때는 ‘No, I don’t mind.(아니오, 신경 쓰지 않아요.)‘ ’Not at all.(전혀요.)‘ ’Of course not.(물론 아니죠.)‘ 등과 같이 부정형으로 답하며, 거절할 때는 ’Yes, I mind.(네, 싫어요.)‘와 같이 긍정형으로 답해야 한다. 대화에서 인도 문화에 대해 설 명을 해 줘도 괜찮을지 묻는 남자의 말에 여자가 ’Of course. (물론이에요.)‘라고 답했고 이어서 남자가 설명을 시작하고 있 으므로, 대화의 흐름상 밑줄 친 ’제가 인도 문화에 관련된 것을 알려드려도 괜찮을까요?‘를 ❸ ’제가 인도 문화에 관련된 것을 알려드리면 싫으실까요?‘로는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate
the importance of small things, often ⓐput them
together to create amazing works of art. Often,
practical need or creative desire plays a key role in
such efforts.
Stitched Together

권에서 오래도록 인정받아 왔으며, 천 조각들을 꿰매
어 더 큰 예술품으로 창조하는 것을 수반하는 바느질
의 한 종류이다. ⓑEvery culture is proud of its own
patterns, including Koreans, who take pride in their
unique style, jogakbo. ⓒCreating during the Joseon
dynasty, it is a type of traditional wrapping cloth
ⓓmade by stitching small pieces of fabric into a
large square or rectangle. Frugal women did not
want to waste any fabric and found ways ⓔto
reuse it. However, jogakbo was ⓕmuch more than
just repurposing fabric. It often told the creator’s
life story because a finished piece contained fabric
scraps from her wedding skirt, her husband’s shirt,
and her children’s clothes. The practical need to
repurpose leftover patches gave birth to a novel art
form.

W: Jim, you seem upset. Is something wrong?
M: Yeah, my pet goldfish is sick. He’s not eating.
W: I’m sorry to hear that. I wish your goldfish were
like immortal jellyfish, which can live forever.
M: Immortal jellyfish? __________________________________
W: When it’s attacked or starved, it transforms itself
into a polyp, which is the previous life stage of
jellyfish.
M: What happens after that?
W: From the polyp, a tiny jellyfish is formed,
starting a new life cycle.
M: So, it’s like a butterfly or a chicken going back
to an egg.
W: That’s right. Immortal jellyfish can keep renewing
themselves, so they can live forever.
M: I wish my goldfish had that incredible ability!

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Have you seen it before?
Where did you learn about it?
Why do you think it is popular?
Can you explain how it can live forever?
How do you take care of such a special fish?
solution: 앞서 여자가 영원히 살 수 있는 불멸의 해파리(immortal jellyfish)에 대해 언급했고, 남자의 반응에 이어 그것이 공격을 받거나 굶으면 해파리 이전의 단계로 스스로를 변화시킨다고 설명하고 있으므로, 남자가 불멸의 해파리가 영원히 살 수 있 는 방법에 대해 구체적으로 설명을 요청하는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘그것이 어떻게 영원히 살 수 있는 지 설명해 줄 수 있어?’가 적절하다.

W: I’m sorry to hear that. I wish your goldfish were
like immortal jellyfish, which can live forever.
M: Immortal jellyfish? __________________________________

into a polyp, which is the previous life stage of
jellyfish.
M: What happens after that?
W: From the polyp, a tiny jellyfish is formed,
starting a new life cycle.

to an egg.
W: That’s right. Immortal jellyfish can keep renewing
themselves, so they can live forever.

Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a ⓐvital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
those that haven’t been specifically bred to live with
humans,
are
also
ⓑwilling
to
form
mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
ⓒmigrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers watch
the dolphins, looking for them to ⓓcommunicate
that they will be making a “deep dive,” which lasts
about 15 seconds. Fishers then cast their nets just
as the dolphins drive the mullets towards the
surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this ⓔcompetition, dolphins may
end up swimming to areas where there aren’t many
fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing
nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
ⓕharmful. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

M: Hey, Kelly. Look at the picture of a bird. What
do you think it’s eating?
W: Oh, that’s a honeyguide bird. It’s eating some
bits of the bee nest.
M: How can it do that without getting attacked by
bees?
W: Well, the bees are not there due to some help
from humans.
M: Really? Can you explain how that works?
W: Well, when a honeyguide bird sees humans in
the forest, it makes a loud noise and guides
them to bee nests.
M: Fascinating! What happens next?
W: Once they find the nest, the humans use smoke
to drive the bees away and collect the honey.
M: Ah, so that’s when the birds can access the
food without getting attacked.
W: Yes. It’s a beautiful partnership between birds
and humans!

how a honeyguide bird avoids being attackedby bees while it accesses the bee nest
what a honeyguide bird does when it spots humansin the forest
what humans do to collect the honey from thebee nest
how humans and bees collaborate with eachother

W: Attention, visitors and residents. The amazing
season of Red Crab Migration on Christmas
Island is back, and sooner or later, millions of
red crabs will be crossing our community from
the forest to the coast to breed or lay eggs.
Their movement peaks in the early mornings
and late afternoons when it’s cooler. Thus, all
visitors and residents are asked to follow a few
guidelines from the wildlife service office during
those hours until the end of this month. First,
it’s necessary to slow down and keep the
speed limit of 30km/h in designated areas. It’s
also necessary to completely stop your vehicle
when you spot crabs on your way. And please
stay tuned to the local radio station because
some roads may be closed. Your cooperation
will ensure the crabs’ safety and allow for our
continued appreciation of their migration every
year.

to explain the scientific reasons why red crabsmigrate every year
to report the results of a study on red crabpopulation changes
to advertise a tourist attraction related to redcrabs on Christmas Island
to inform people about the red crab migrationand what people should do during that period

In a suburb in the Pacific Northwest, Justin ties his
shoes for his morning run and steps out at dawn.
As he walks off his front step, he spots some
racoons crossing the street. Up in a tree, he sees a
family of squirrels. Birds begin to sing, and he
enjoys the beauty of his neighborhood. ⓐWhile
running, a dangerous sight interrupts the idyllic
scene. A coyote watches as a black bear searches
through a garbage bin for food. Justin is surprised
at his neighborhood transforming into a place ⓑfull
of wildlife encounters.
Why Animals Migrate to Cities
In 2019, it was estimated that more than 1.5 million
squirrels were living in Chicago and ⓒapproximately
10,000 foxes in London. In Seoul, 155 wild boars
were captured in 2022. Why are there so many
animals in big cities? One reason is that many cities
are built on biologically fertile and productive land
areas, which are attractive not only to humans but to
other creatures as well. (A)또 다른 이유는 도시 지역들
이 더욱 녹지화 되면서, 더 많은 야생 동물들을 유인하
기 때문이다. Cities have begun building more gardens,
parks, and legally protected areas for educational,
recreational, or other purposes, ⓓattracting more
wild creatures. In addition, for some animal species,
cities have become a perfect place for feeding,
mating, and nesting. Peregrine falcons, for example,
use tall buildings for nesting sites, man-made
lighting to hunt for prey at night, and warm urban
air currents to soar easily. Cities have become
home, sweet home, ⓔnot only to humans but to
wild animals.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: While he runs
ⓑ: which is full of wildlife encounters
ⓒ: approximately 10,000 foxes to live in London
ⓓ: and they have attracted more wild creatures
ⓔ: to wild animals as well as to humans
solution: ⓒ ‘주어+동사+부사구’로 이루어진 완전한 절 ‘more than 1.5 million squirrels were living in Chicago’ 뒤에 등위접속사 and로 연결되어 있으므로 ‘주어+동사+부사구’ 형태의 절에서 반복되는 동사구 were living이 생략된 형태이다. 따라서 approximately 10,000 foxes to live in London이 아니라 ‘approximately 10,000 foxes were living in London’으로 전환해야 한다.

increased
populations.

choices: sothatnature will

solution: (A) 명사구 a destructive control method를 수식하므로 한정사 such가 적절하다. 참고로, such는 명사구를 수식해 ‘such+a(n)+ (형용사+)가산단수명사(구)’ 또는 ‘such+(형용사+)복수명사(구)’ 어순을 이루며, 부사인 so는 형용사[분사]와 부사를 수식한다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(prevents ~ breeding)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a strict structure를 수식하는 관계사절을 이 루어야 하므로, 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. 참고로, 관계 부사 where는 완전한 절을 이끈다. (C) how 이하는 동사 predict의 목적어로 쓰인 간접의문문이므 로, 의문사 how 뒤에 ‘주어+조동사+동사원형~’의 평서문 어순 이 되어야 한다. 따라서 ‘주어+조동사’의 순서로 쓰인 nature will이 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) 3과

body:
Coyotes and racoons cause conflicts with residents
in many towns in North America. Elephants damage
crops and property in Africa. Wild boars destroy
agricultural fields in Asia and Europe. The idea that
wild animals are annoyances or threats that need to
be eliminated is common in many parts of the
world. However, often, unintended consequences
occur because of this attitude. A balanced approach
is needed, particularly between human safety and
the well-being of the animals, which can be found
when we grasp a proper understanding of their
behavior as well as their role in their natural
habitat. After all, we should acknowledge the fact
that both humans and animals are temporary
tenants of this precious planet. Neither is less
valuable nor more valuable than the other. _________
_____________________________________ is the only choice.

choices: Human dominance over nature
Eliminating dangerous species to ensure humansafety
Maintaining balance and harmony among all livingspecies
Finding a quick solution that focuses mainly onreducing human inconvenience
Developing long-term strategies that prioritizeeconomic growth over ecological responsibility

only capital with a national park, which attracts
many international tourists with wild lions and other
beasts against the backdrop of tall buildings in its
urban center.
(A) He devised the lights to flicker on and off from
time to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed
his first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again,
and his family didn’t lose any cattle to them.
(B) Living near the park, a thirteen-year-old boy named
Richard Turere was responsible for keeping his
family’s cattle safe from lions that often came out
of the park at night to hunt. Many neighbors had
lost their cows, and others their goats and sheep.
(C) Neighbors followed suit, protecting their valuable
source of income without killing the unwanted
neighbors. This is an example of a keen observation
on animal behavior leading to a creative approach
that brought peace and harmony.

discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and didn’t come near the cattle enclosure when
he walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure facing the outside and connected them
to an old car battery powered by a solar panel.

Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
ⓐthose that haven’t been specifically bred to live
with humans, are also willing to form mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive ⓑthem towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch ⓒthem with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
ⓓthem
to
communicate that ⓔthey will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end
up swimming to areas where there aren’t many fish,
and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of (A)_____________________________
_______________________________________________________.
This harmony has kept the tradition alive for
generations, and it continues to inspire us today.

M: Minji, isn’t your new English teacher coming this
week from America?

I call him by his first name, to say “Welcome,
Marcus!”?

someone for the first time, it’s polite to call
them by their title and last name.

use his first name.
W: Thanks for letting me know. I’ll remember that
whenever I meet someone new.
M: Okay. But when a person is around your age or
younger, you can use their first name.
W: It’s somewhat similar to Korean etiquette!

A Journey to Samoa
Samoa is a Polynesian island country, ⓐconsisting
of two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in
the South Pacific. It is known for its year-round
warm
tropical
weather,
stunning
beaches,
and
gorgeous waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of
the sources of inspiration for the directors of the
movie Moana released in 2016. It is a stunning
island country ⓑin which preserves its traditions,
history, and distinct way of life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, ⓒsupported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate.
(A)그것의 옆이 개방된 구조는 공기가 자유롭게 순환
하게 하여 공간을 계속 시원하게 할 뿐만 아니라 강한
바람이 빠져나갈 수 있도록 하여 그것이 극한 날씨를
견뎌낼 수 있도록 해준다. The unique structure of
the fale mirrors the Samoan people’s values of
openness and community. Its open structure allows
people ⓓcome and go freely, creating a sense of
belonging.
Samoans Were Time Travelers
Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries ⓔused to being in the same time zone,
the situation completely changed in 2011. On
December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped December 30,
and went straight to December 31, ⓕjumped 24
hours into the future. This happened because the
Samoan government decided to switch sides of the
International Date Line. This was ⓖto align the time
with New Zealand, Australia, and other Asian
countries, to improve their business transactions.
Samoa is now on the opposite side of the
International Date Line from American Samoa. They
are just half an hour apart by flight, but there is a
24-hour time difference between them. If you fly
from Samoa to American Samoa, in about 30
minutes you will return to yesterday!

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ in which → that[which] (동사 preserves의 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(preserves ~ life) 를 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 a stunning island country를 수식 하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 완전한 절 앞에 쓰이는 ’전 치사+관계대명사‘ 형태의 in which를 선행사에 어울리는 주격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.) ⓓ come → to come (‘~가 …하게 하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘allow+목적어+목적격보어’의 5 형식 구문에 쓰일 때 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므 로, allows와 목적어 people에 이어진 목적격보어 자리의 동사 원형 come을 to부정사인 to come으로 고친다.) ⓔ used to being → used to be (접속사 Although의 양보 부사절에서, 주어 these two countries의 동사 used to에 이어져 ’(예전에는) ~였다(지금은 아니다)‘라는 뜻으로 과거의 상태를 나타내는 ’used to+동사원 형‘을 이루어야 하므로, being을 동사원형 be로 고친다.) ⓕ jumped → jumping (앞의 동사구(went ~ 31)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사 구가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 동시상황을 나타내는 분사구 문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 주절 주어와 동일한 분 사구문의 의미상 주어 Samoans가 ‘뛰어넘은’ 주체이므로, jumped를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 jumping으로 고친다.)

“Good things come in small packages,” they say.

the importance of small things, often putting them

Stitched Together
Patchwork,
whose
beauty
has
long
been
appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a
type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of
fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every
culture is proud of its own patterns, including
Koreans, who take pride in their unique style,
jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a
type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching
small pieces of fabric into a large square or
rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste any
fabric and found ways to reuse it. However,

finished piece contained fabric scraps from her
wedding

her
husband’s
shirt,

her
children’s clothes. The practical need to repurpose

the influence of modern fashion trends
the use of expensive decorative techniques

(B) 기혼 여성은 구슬 목걸이, 구슬 망토와 더불어 다섯 개의 판으로 이루어진 앞치마를 입으며, 아직 결혼을 하지 않은 소 녀는 수천 개의 유리구슬을 손으로 꿰매어 만든 정사각형의 앞치마를 입을 수 있다는 내용이 언급되어 있으므로, 남아프 리카의 Ndebele(은데벨레) 부족은 유리구슬로 만든 복잡한 의 복으로 유명하다고 소개하는 흐름으로 intricate(복잡한)가 적 절하다. (C) 남아프리카의 Ndebele(은데벨레) 부족의 구슬 공예 전통에 대한 예시에 이어 Similarly(이와 비슷하게)를 사용해 유사한 또 다른 예시를 소개하는 흐름이며, 구슬 공예는 수 세대에 걸친 지속성을 반영하며 문화적 정체성을 강하게 표현한다는 구체 적 설명이 뒤에 이어지므로, 많은 아메리카 원주민 문화에서도 중요한 측면이라는 흐름으로 essential(필수적인, 중요한)이 적 절하다.

A Journey to Samoa
Samoa is a Polynesian island country, ⓐconsisting
of two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in
the South Pacific. It is known for its year-round
warm
tropical
weather,
stunning
beaches,
and
gorgeous waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of
the sources of inspiration for the directors of the
movie Moana released in 2016. It is a stunning
island country ⓑin which preserves its traditions,
history, and distinct way of life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, ⓒsupported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate.
(A)그것의 옆이 개방된 구조는 공기가 자유롭게 순환
하게 하여 공간을 계속 시원하게 할 뿐만 아니라 강한
바람이 빠져나갈 수 있도록 하여 그것이 극한 날씨를
견뎌낼 수 있도록 해준다. The unique structure of
the fale mirrors the Samoan people’s values of
openness and community. Its open structure allows
people ⓓcome and go freely, creating a sense of
belonging.
Samoans Were Time Travelers
Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries ⓔused to being in the same time zone,
the situation completely changed in 2011. On
December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped December 30,
and went straight to December 31, ⓕjumped 24
hours into the future. This happened because the
Samoan government decided to switch sides of the
International Date Line. This was ⓖto align the time
with New Zealand, Australia, and other Asian
countries, to improve their business transactions.
Samoa is now on the opposite side of the
International Date Line from American Samoa. They
are just half an hour apart by flight, but there is a
24-hour time difference between them. If you fly
from Samoa to American Samoa, in about 30
minutes you will return to yesterday!

Stitched Together
Patchwork,
whose
beauty
has
long
been
appreciated in many cultures across the globe, is a
type of needlework that involves sewing scraps of
fabric together to create a larger piece of art. Every
culture is proud of its own patterns, including
Koreans, who take pride in their unique style,
jogakbo. Created during the Joseon dynasty, it is a
type of traditional wrapping cloth made by stitching
small pieces of fabric into a large square or
rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste any
fabric and found ways to reuse it. However,
jogakbo was much more than just repurposing
fabric. It often told the creator’s life story because a
finished piece contained fabric scraps from her
wedding
skirt,
her
husband’s
shirt,
and
her
children’s clothes. The practical need to repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.
The beauty of jogakbo lies in its design, which
results from stitching together patches of various
shapes, sizes, and colors in a seemingly improvised
manner. Stitching such random patches into a
perfect
square
or
rectangle
requires
artistic
sensitivity, a high level of skill, careful planning, and
long
hours
stitching.
The
desire
for
creative
excellence resulted in harmonious combinations of
patches in various colors, shapes, and sizes, which
have been compared to modern abstract paintings,
such as those of Piet Mondrian or Paul Klee.
Jogakbo was a useful activity in which ______________
________________________________________________________,
eventually becoming an important part of traditional
Korean craft art.
choices: fabric pieces were arranged mainly for ceremonialdecoration
repeated traditional patterns were used to expresscultural identity
symbolic meanings were emphasized more thanpractical purposes
artistic techniques were formally taught byprofessional craftsmen
leftover pieces of cloth were transformed into apursuit of beauty and utility

The Sainte-Chapelle in Paris, France and Nasir
al-Mulk mosque in Shiraz, Iran amaze their visitors
with brilliant glass window panels through which
astonishing light of vigorous colors penetrates.
These panels are called stained-glass windows and
are made up of colored pieces of glass assembled
together to form large windows.
(A) Small pieces of glass assembled next to one
another were not only more practical for
construction but also able to tell a story.
(B) Since most people were illiterate at that time,
the images placed on the windows helped them
understand religious messages that they might
otherwise have been unable to grasp.
(C) In Europe and the Middle East, the techniques
for
stained-glass windows
advanced
quickly
during the Medieval period, when religious
buildings got bigger to accommodate more
worshipers and prayers.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 프랑스 파리의 Sainte-Chapelle(생트 샤펠)과 이란의 시라즈에 있는 Nasir al-Mulk(나시르 알 물크) 사원의 스테인드글라스 창에 대해 소개하는 주어진 글에 이어, 종교 시설의 크기가 커 지고 있던 유럽과 중동의 중세 시기를 언급하며 스테인드글라 스 창을 만드는 기술의 발달 배경을 설명하는 (C), 스테인드글 라스 창의 기술인 나란히 짜맞추어진 유리 조각들의 장점으로, 건축에 있어서 실용적이었을 뿐 아니라 이야기를 전달하는 기 능도 했다는 측면을 언급하는 (A), 앞서 언급된 이야기 전달 기능과 관련해서, 그리고 (C)에서 언급된 중세 시대를 지칭하 는 at that time에 의해, 당시 대부분의 사람들이 문맹이었기 때문에 창에 표현된 이미지가 종교적인 메시지를 이해할 수 있도록 도와주었다고 부연하는 (B)로 이어지는 것이 적절하다.

line or paying a premium : ⓑ 동명사구 주어(promoting values)는 단수 취급하므로 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친다. ‘~을 창출하는’이 라는 뜻으로 명사구 an important strategy를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to create는 적절하다. ⓒ do not know의 목적어 자리에 be동사 are의 보어가 없는 불완전한 절(their values are)이 왔으므로, 완전한 절을 이끌어 명사절을 이루는 접속사 that은 적절하지 않다. are의 보어 역할을 하면서 ‘무엇’이라는 뜻으로 간 접의문문을 이끄는 의문대명사 what으로 고쳐야 한다. 간접의문문은 ‘의문사(구)+평서문’ 어순을 이루므로, what 뒤에 주어 their values와 동사 are가 차례대로 오는 것 은 적절하다. ⓓ 완전한 절(consumers ~ premium)을 이끌어 동사 hear의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다. 흐름상 ‘소비자들이 줄 을 서고 있거나 프리미엄을 지불하고 있다’라는 뜻으로 be동사 are와 함께 쓰여 현재진행형을 이루는 현재분사 standing과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 동사원형 pay를 현재분사 paying으로 고친다. 11) ③: 기업이 개인화된 마케팅을 통해 소비자와 신뢰를 형성 하고 소비자가 원하는 것을 파악하는 방식을 설명하는 글이다. 구체적으로, 밈 마케팅은 특정 집단이 공감할 수 있는 메시지를 전달하여 소비자에게 소속감과 신뢰 를 형성하게 하며, 소셜 미디어 인플루언서는 제품 홍 보를 통해 기업이 소비자 피드백과 요구를 파악하도록 돕는다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 제목으로 적 절한 것은 ③ ‘개인화가 브랜드가 소비자의 신뢰를 구 축하는 데 어떻게 도움이 되는가’이다. 오답 ① 마케팅의 발전: 오프라인에서 소셜 미디어로 ② 소셜 미디어 마케팅이 더욱 인기를 얻고 있는 이유 ④ 피드백을 수집하기 위한 도구로서 소셜 미디어 인 플루언서를 활용하기 ⑤ 누구에게나 다 맞는 제품이 현대 비즈니스에서도 여전히 비용 효율적인 이유 12) ①: 현대의 마케팅은 복잡하지만, 과거에는 가정의 필요가 비슷하고 이를 생산하여 판매하는 기업도 적어 마케팅 이 비교적 단순했으며, 과거에는 인쇄 광고, 방송, 방문 판매와 같은 오프라인 방식이 유용한 제품을 홍보하는 비용 효율적인 수단이었지만, 오늘날에는 기술 발전과 소비자 행동 분석으로 마케팅 방식이 크게 변화하였다 는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ① ‘단순한 전통적 마케팅에서 데이터 기반의 복잡한 현대 마케팅으로의 변화’이다. 오답 ② 소비자 생활방식을 형성하는 데 있어 가전제품의 중요성 증가 ③ 현대 기술이 기업들이 소비자에게 접근하는 방식을 어떻게 단순화했는지 ④ 디지털 마케팅에 비해 오프라인 광고 방식의 장점 ⑤ 현대에 마케팅 비용을 줄이기 위한 효과적인 전략들 13) ③: 차례대로 T-T-F-F이다. (A) 제한된 수의 제조업체들이 과거의 덜 복잡한 마케 팅에 기여했다. (T) (일치) (B) 전통적인 오프라인 방식은 실용적인 상품들을 홍보 하는 데 효율적이었다. (T) (일치) (C) 현대의 마케팅은 새로운 기술과 비즈니스 전략의 변화 때문에 더 단순해졌다(→복잡해졌다). (F) (불일치) (D) 기술이 발전함에 따라 전통적인 오프라인 마케팅 방식은 더욱 비용 효율적이 되었다.(→마케팅이 극적으 로 변화하고 있다.) (F) (불일치) 14) ④: (A) 기업이 ‘욕구’를 창출하는 마케팅의 예시를 설명하 고 있으므로 가치를 홍보하는 것도 수요를 ‘창출하는’ 중요한 전략이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 기존의 존재하 는 수요를 충족(satisfy)시키는 것이 아니라 새로운 수 요를 창출한다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 create(창출하 다)가 적절하다. satisfy ~을 충족시키다 (B) 뒤에 이어지는 예시에서 환경적 대의를 지지하는 회사는 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다고 했으므로 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 ‘일치하 는’ 브랜드를 선택한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 aligned(일치하는)이 적절하다. conflicted 상충된 (C) 뒤에 제시된 예시 문장에서 소비자들이 줄을 서거 나 프리미엄을 지불하고 있다는 것을 사람들이 들을 때 제품에 대한 욕구는 커질 것이라고 했으므로 ‘심리’ 를 이용해 수요를 유발한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 psychology(심리)가 적절하다. rationality 합리성 15) ②: ⓑ, ⓒ는 their customers(기업들의 고객)를 가리킨다. 오답 ⓐ Businesses ⓓ Businesses ⓔ Big brands ⓕ Big brands 16) marketing, data, preferences, optimize 요약문 마케팅이 오프라인에서 온라인으로 확장됨에 따라, 기업들은 특정 고객 집단에 도달하기 위해 웹사이트, 인플 루언서, 그리고 제품 배치와 같은 새로운 도구들을 사용했 으며, 소비자들의 온라인 행동에서 얻은 데이터는 그들이 소비자 선호도를 알아내고 마케팅 노력을 최적화하는 것도 가능하게 했다. 17) ①: ⓐ what → that (완전한 절(it ~ their brand)을 이끌어 동사 realized의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓑ 동사 commissioned, 목적어 Warhol에 이어지는 목 적격보어 자리로, 동사 commission은 ‘commission+목 적어+to부정사(목적격보어)’의 5형식 구조로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리에 to create는 적절하다. ⓒ 주어 celebrity exposure가 ‘사용되는’ 대상이므로 조 동사 can 뒤에 수동태(be p.p.)가 와야 한다. 따라서 동 사원형 be와 함께 수동태를 이루는 과거분사 used는 적절하다. ⓓ ‘찾기 위해’라는 목적의 뜻을 갖는 부사적 용법의 to 부정사 to find와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 create는 적절하다. ⓔ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 to부정사 to decide는 적절하다. 18) ②: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 예시 문장에서 환경적 대의를 지지 하는 회사는 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다고 했으므로 많은 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 ‘일치하는’ 브랜드를 선택한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따 라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 matches(일치한 다), fits(부합한다)이다. 본문변형 is aligned with → matches (B) 앞에서 소비자가 자신의 가치관이 무엇인지 모를 때는 심리를 이용해 수요를 유발한다고 했으므로 소비 자들이 줄을 서거나 프리미엄을 지불하고 있다는 것을 사람들이 들을 때 제품에 대한 욕구가 ‘커질 것이다’라 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적 절한 것은 intensify(강해지다), increase(증가하다)이다. 본문변형 grow → intensify 오답 ① 일치한다  감소하다 ③ 모순된다  강해지다 ④ 부합한다  감소하다 ⑤ 모순된다  증가하다

W: Leo, what is that?
M: This is my stamp collection. I’ve collected over
700 stamps so far.
W: Amazing! Why do you collect stamps?
M: Well, I like learning about historical events through
stamp designs. For example, a Gutenberg printing
press from the 15th century is printed on this stamp.
W: A Gutenberg printing press? ______________________
_____________________
M: It was an important invention that helped people
learn how to read and write.
W: How so?
M: Before the printing press, all writings and drawings
were copied by hand. Professional copyists
worked in small rooms to copy ancient books.
W: I can’t imagine how long it must have taken to
copy an entire book by hand.
M: It took days to make a single book.
W: Books were probably too expensive for ordinary
people to own long ago.
M: Right! The printing press allowed people to make
books quickly, cheaply, and in large numbers.
W: What a revolution!

choices: What makes it so special?
Did people oppose it at the beginning?
How does it affect modern education today?
What role did it play in spreading knowledge?
Why is it considered controversial among historians?

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

One
of
the
most
noticeable
and
effective
applications is real-time monitoring of fish behavior
and other environmental changes, which serves
multiple purposes, including diagnosing diseases in
individual fish.
(A) The right amount of food at the right time
minimizes cost, reduces waste and pollution,
and maximizes fish growth rates. Given the fact
that feeding constitutes more than 50% of a
fish farm’s operational budget, this precise
feeding approach will ultimately contribute to a
more affordable supply of fish for consumers as
well as efficient and sustainable aquaculture
operations in general.
(B) The system can also tell farmers exactly when to
feed the fish by identifying patterns of behavior
that an individual fish or the school exhibits
when they are hungry. This is how farmers can
accurately determine optimal feeding times and
amounts.
(C) By processing large sets of data, an AI system
can detect and recognize unusual group behaviors
of an entire school of fish, possibly caused by
changes in water quality, temperature, or oxygen
levels surrounding the cage. It can also ensure
the quality of cage nets to prevent fish from
escaping or predators from invading and protect
the surrounding habitat.

body:
Museums are said to be places where time is
transformed into space. Maybe that’s why people
visit them, to learn and be inspired in new ways.
Accordingly, museums are adopting new techniques
and technologies to meet the diverse demands of
visitors.
To help visitors interact with artworks and artists
in a novel, engaging way, many museums are
adopting technology to enhance the experience of
museum-goers.
The
Van
Gogh
Museum
in
Amsterdam allows visitors to virtually touch objects
and interact with the characters inside, immersing
themselves in the artworks.
Some museums are even personalizing services, as
natural language processing techniques can be
implemented into chatbots. The chatbot of the
British Museum of London explains details not only

(A)[in which / which] businesses or organizations

also be used for other specific objectives, such as
boosting brand awareness, building customer loyalty,

washing machines, televisions, and rice cookers.

every household needed to clean their clothes, watch
the news, and cook food, and few companies could
make and sell products that could perform those
tasks. Print advertisements, broadcasting, door-to-door
sales, and other offline methods were cost-effective
ways to market products that people found useful.
However, marketing has dramatically changed in
present times as businesses utilize new technology,
analyze consumer behavior, and shift business strategies.

for
their
brand.

range of instruments to analyze consumer
needs and stimulate demand. (T/F)

strategy
rather
than
combining
multiple
marketing methods. (T/F)

own judgments regarding the vast amount of
marketing information. (T/F)

Stitched Together
Patchwork, whose beauty has long been appreciated
in many cultures across the globe, is a type of
needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric
together to create a larger piece of art. Every culture
is proud of its own patterns, including Koreans, who
take pride in their unique style, jogakbo. Created
during the Joseon dynasty, it is a type of traditional
wrapping cloth made by stitching small pieces of
fabric into a large square or rectangle. Frugal women
did not want to waste any fabric and found ways to
reuse it. However, jogakbo was much more than just
repurposing fabric. It often told the creator’s life
story because a finished piece contained fabric scraps
from her wedding skirt, her husband’s shirt, and her
children’s clothes. The practical need to repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.
The beauty of jogakbo lies in its design, which
results from stitching together patches of various
shapes, sizes, and colors in a seemingly improvised
manner. Stitching such random patches into a perfect
square or rectangle requires artistic sensitivity, a
high level of skill, careful planning, and long hours
stitching. The desire for creative excellence resulted
in harmonious combinations of patches in various
colors, shapes, and sizes, which have been compared
to modern abstract paintings, such as those of Piet
Mondrian or Paul Klee. Jogakbo was a useful activity
in which leftover pieces of cloth were transformed into
a pursuit of beauty and utility, eventually becoming
an important part of traditional Korean craft art.
choices: Patchwork, a type of sewing, is the activity inwhich pieces of fabric are stitched together tocreate a larger work of art.
Thrifty women in the Joseon Dynasty reused fabricto make jogakbo in order to avoid wasting anycloth.
A new art form like jogakbo was born from thepractical need to recycle leftover fabric pieces.
Skilled artisans can sew random fabric piecesinto perfect squares or rectangles using onlytheir natural artistic sense.
Jogakbo, recognized for its unique patterns, hasbecome an crucial part of Korea’s traditionalcraft art.

Samoa is a Polynesian island country, consisting of
two main islands (Upolu and Savai’i), located in the
South Pacific. It is known for its year-round warm
tropical weather, stunning beaches, and gorgeous
waterfalls. Samoa even served as one of the sources
of inspiration for the directors of the movie Moana
released in 2016. It is a stunning island country that
preserves its traditions, history, and distinct way of
life.
Samoans Have No Walls
A “fale” is a traditional Samoan house, with
round-shaped thatched huts, supported by wood
columns, but with no walls. The architecture of fale
is very well-suited to the Samoan tropical climate. Its
open-sided structure not only allows air to circulate
freely to keep the space cool but also allows strong
winds to pass through, enabling it to resist extreme
weather events. The unique structure of the fale
mirrors the Samoan people’s values of openness
and community. Its open structure allows people to
come and go freely, creating a sense of belonging.

the structural advantages of the “fale”

Samoa
and
American
Samoa
are
different
countries, even though they are next to each other
in the South Pacific Ocean. Although these two
countries used to be in the same time zone, the
situation completely changed in 2011.
(A) This was to align the time with New Zealand,
Australia, and other Asian countries, to improve
their business transactions. Samoa is now on
the opposite side of the International Date Line
from American Samoa.
(B) They are just half an hour apart by flight, but
there is a 24-hour time difference between
them. If you fly from Samoa to American
Samoa, in about 30 minutes you will return to
yesterday!
(C) On December 29, 2011, Samoans skipped
December 30, and went straight to December
31, jumping 24 hours into the future. This
happened because the Samoan government
decided to switch sides of the International
Date Line.

visit them, to learn and be inspired in new ways.

and technologies to meet the diverse demands of
visitors.

in a novel, engaging way, many museums are
adopting technology to (A)[enrich / standardize] the
experience
of
museum-goers.

Van
Gogh
Museum in Amsterdam allows visitors to virtually
touch objects and interact with the characters
inside, immersing themselves in the artworks.
Some museums are even personalizing services, as
natural language processing techniques can be
implemented into chatbots. The chatbot of the
British Museum of London explains details not only
about the exhibits but also about the facilities and
venues, in a dozen different languages.
Personalized services will continue to be an
important part of a museum visitor’s experience.

(C) 방문객의 시선을 추적하고 무엇이 그들을 흥미롭게 하는지 를 식별하며 개인 맞춤화된 관람을 추천한다는 내용에 이어지 므로, 방문객의 참여를 유도하는 퀴즈를 제공한다는 흐름으로 participatory(참여형의, 참여를 유도하는)가 알맞다.

body:
Museums are said to be places where time is
transformed into space. Maybe that’s why people
visit them, to learn and be inspired in new ways.
Accordingly, museums are adopting new techniques
and technologies to meet the diverse demands of
visitors.
To help visitors interact with artworks and artists
in a novel, engaging way, many museums are
adopting technology to (A)[enrich / standardize] the
experience
of
museum-goers.
The
Van
Gogh
Museum in Amsterdam allows visitors to virtually
touch objects and interact with the characters
inside, immersing themselves in the artworks.
Some museums are even personalizing services, as
natural language processing techniques can be
implemented into chatbots. The chatbot of the
British Museum of London explains details not only
about the exhibits but also about the facilities and
venues, in a dozen different languages.
Personalized services will continue to be an
important part of a museum visitor’s experience.
Based on an analysis of a visitors’ background and
(B)[future / past] behavior, including the artworks,
websites, or social media sites they’ve viewed or
given a “like” to online, deep learning systems can
predict and recommend artworks they would most
likely be interested in. The National Museum of
Singapore conducted a study in 2017 on developing
a deep learning engine that can track a visitor’s
gaze, identify what interests them, recommend
personalized tours, and show them virtual objects
on
top
of
real-world
exhibits,
often
giving
(C)[one-way / participatory] quizzes and games that
suit their interests.
To some, visiting museums and galleries may be a
way of escaping from everyday dullness. To others,
it may be a serious attempt to enter a world of
beauty,
wonder,
imagination,
and
inspiration.
Whatever their reasons are, more visitors will seek a
unique way of appreciating the exhibits, and more
innovative services will emerge.

윗글을 아래와 같이 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Museums use ⓐ______________ technologies to
create interactive, personalized experiences for
visitors and will continue to ⓑ______________ their
services.
ⓐ                   ⓑ
choices: innovativesimplify
outdatedgeneralize
advanceddevelop
conventionalexpand
novelevaluate
solution: 정답은 ③ 이다. (해설 없음)

An essential element in providing healthy fish to
consumers is the fish farmers’ ability to detect and
prevent sea lice, a significant threat to fish health
and profitability. One of the most modern methods
to do this is through the power of computer vision
and precision sensors, allowing fish farmers to
identify and track diseases before they spread. An
aquaculture system equipped with high-precision
underwater tools has already been developed in
Norway. (A)그것은 고해상도 카메라와 센서가 각각의
연어에 대한 모든 것을 기록하는 튜브 안으로 각각의
물고기를 정기적으로 유도하며, 15만 마리까지의 연어
를 바다 가두리에 보관할 수 있다, including their
overall shapes and dot patterns, their weight and
growth rate, as well as any signs of sea lice,
physical wounds, or abnormalities. Every detail is
registered in the fish’s health record, along with
millions of images and figures. Such huge amounts
of data and other information are taken care of by
the AI system.

AI continues to advance in aquaculture to extend
beyond caged fish. In particular, smart fish farming
technologies can be applied to seaweed farming.
Seaweed is as valuable a source of food as fish. It’s
also a source of fuel and an important ingredient
for cosmetics, fertilizers, and other medicinal and
industrial products. As such, ongoing research is
exploring various ways AI can help in the seaweed
industry,
including
the
use
of
autonomous
underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm robotics.
Using cameras and sensors, AUVs can do many of
the analytical and diagnostic tasks on seaweed
farms. Swarm robots, or many small robots working
together, can swim in and around seaweed farms to
collect data and then make decisions on how to
deal with problems that arise. Single larger robots
or even humans may be available to take care of
the physical labor from removing harmful weeds to
harvesting; however, swarm robots may be more
efficient and cost-effective.

The Declining Importance of Seaweed in ModernAquaculture

Seaweed Farming as a Minor Area of TechnologicalDevelopment
The Expanding Role of AI Technologies in SeaweedFarming Management

M: Look! This is my favorite designer’s new release.
W: It’s amazing! Isn’t that a gat the model is
wearing?
M: Yes. I’m surprised you know what a gat is.
W: When I first saw one on a Korean historical TV
show, it looked so cool that I looked it up. It’s
made of horsehair, right?
M: Right! Then, _______________________________________?
W: No, I haven’t. What’s that?
M: It’s another kind of traditional Korean hat. It
looks similar to a gat, but it’s made of bamboo
strips instead.
W: Was it only worn by men like in the TV show?
M: Yes. Back then, women didn’t usually wear hats
like a gat or paeraengi.
W: That’s very interesting. I’m going to look for a
gat online. I think it would look good on me.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: have you heard of paeraengi
have you worn a gat in public
have you seen the designer’s older works
have you bought a traditional Korean hat
have you watched another historical TV show

“Good things come in small packages,” they say.
Indeed, some cultures around the world appreciate
the importance of small things, often putting them
together to create amazing works of art. Often,
practical need or creative desire ⓐplays a key role
in such efforts.
Stitched Together
Patchwork, whose beauty ⓑhas long appreciated
in many cultures across the globe, is a type of
needlework that involves sewing scraps of fabric
together to create a larger piece of art. Every
culture is proud of its own patterns, including
Koreans, ⓒwhich take pride in their unique style,
jogakbo. ⓓCreated during the Joseon dynasty, it is
a type of traditional wrapping cloth made by
stitching small pieces of fabric into a large square
or rectangle. Frugal women did not want to waste
any fabric and ⓔfind ways to reuse it. However,
jogakbo was much more than just repurposing
fabric. It often told the creator’s life story because a
finished piece contained fabric scraps from her
wedding
skirt,
her
husband’s
shirt,
and
her
children’s clothes. The practical need ⓕto repurpose
leftover patches gave birth to a novel art form.

body:
Strung Together
Throughout the ages and across all cultures, there
have been small decorative objects with a hole for
threading
called
beads.
In
its
simplest
form,
beadwork can involve threading a few beads
together on a single string to make a simple
bracelet or necklace, or on a larger scale, to form
beaded
bags,
clothing,
or
even
wall-hangings.
Beadwork is ancient, evidenced by the findings of
beads dating back to the Stone Age. Back then,
people strung bones, shells, or rocks together to
hang around their neck. As cultures and societies
evolved over time, beadwork became a form of
personal expression, a symbol of social class, or
even a talisman to drive away bad luck.
Interestingly, some regions have particularly rich
traditions. The Ndebele tribe of South Africa,
ⓐ_______________, is famed for intricate dresses made
of glass beads. Different designs serve as a means
of marking different developmental stages of a
woman’s life. An unmarried girl may wear a square
apron onto which thousands of glass beads were
hand-sewn, while a married woman might wear a
five-paneled apron, along with beaded necklaces
and a beaded cape. ⓑ_______________, beadwork is
an essential aspect of many Native American
cultures. Beadwork powerfully expresses cultural
identity, reflecting a sense of continuity across
generations.

윗글의 첫 번째 단락의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Beadwork has been limited to simple jewelrysuch as necklaces and bracelets.
Beads were mainly used in ancient times asprotective objects against physical danger.
Beadwork evolved through a long history acrossdifferent cultures, playing various symbolic roles.
The materials used in beadwork changed completelyas societies became more advanced.
Beadwork spread rapidly across cultures onlyafter the development of modern societies.
solution: 구슬 공예는 여러 시대와 모든 문화권에서 다양한 규모와 형 태로 존재하며 오랜 역사를 거쳐 발달해 왔으며, 개인적 표현 의 형태나 사회적 계급의 상징, 악운을 쫓아내는 부적과 같이 사회와 문화에서 상징적 역할을 해왔다는 내용이므로, 글의 요 지로 ❸ ‘구슬 공예는 다양한 문화에서 오랜 역사를 거쳐 발전 하며 다양한 상징적 역할을 해 왔다.’가 적절하다.

solution: (A) 부분들의 단순한 합보다 더 아름답고 실용적인 새로운 형태의 창조적인 작품을 만든다는 설명이 이어지므로, 작고 단순하며 중요하지 않은 물건을 이용해 큰 의미를 갖는 예술을 창조한 다는 흐름으로 insignificant(중요하지 않은, 사소한)가 적절하다. (B) The Greek philosopher(그 그리스의 철학자)는 글 초반에 언급된 플라톤을 가리키며, 그가 ‘우리의 필요가 진정한 창조자 가 될 것입니다.‘라고 말했고, 이에 대해 필요성이나 갈망에 생 기면 공동체들이 일상의 물체들을 붙여서 더 아름답고 실용적 인 작품을 창조한다고 설명하고 있으므로, 그가 모든 창의적인 것을 위한 과정은 (주변에서) 구할 수 있는 물건들의 유용성을 극대화하기 위해 시작된다는 사실을 인식했을지도 모른다는 흐름으로 maximize(~을 극대화하다)가 적절하다. (C) 문화들은 표면적으로는 달라 보일 수도 있다는 내용 뒤에 but(그러나)으로 대조적인 내용이 연결되어야 하므로, 그것들은 대개 보편적이고 본질적인 공통의 요소를 공유하는 것 같다는 흐름으로 share(공유하다)가 적절하다. 비상(홍민표) 2과

The Sainte-Chapelle in Paris, France and Nasir
al-Mulk mosque in Shiraz, Iran amaze their visitors
with brilliant glass window panels through which
astonishing light of vigorous colors penetrates. These
panels are called stained-glass windows and are
made up of colored pieces of glass assembled
together to form large windows. In Europe and the
Middle
East,
the
techniques
for
stained-glass
windows advanced quickly during the Medieval
period, when religious buildings got bigger to
accommodate more worshipers and prayers. Small
pieces of glass assembled next to one another were
not only more practical for construction but also
able to tell a story. Since most people were illiterate
at that time, the images placed on the windows
helped them understand religious messages that
they might otherwise have been unable to grasp.
Making a stained-glass window is a process in
which intricacy is required. It involves creating
durable glass sheets and staining them, cutting
them into desired shapes, and assembling them into
prepared
designs.
Each
step
requires
expert
craftspeople working together. Though originally
used in religious structures, stained-glass windows
found their way into a variety of modern buildings,
including residential homes. These little pieces are
now recognized worldwide as an important form of
creative art, whose splendor wouldn’t have been
acknowledged without ________________________________.
choices: advances in industrial technology during themodern era
public appreciation for decorative art in non-religiousspaces
formal training systems established for professionalcraftsmen
the glass artists’ desire for beauty sparked by apractical need
the influence of changing architectural trends inmodern society

Strung Together
Throughout the ages and across all cultures, there
have been small decorative objects with a hole for
threading
called
beads.
In
its
simplest
form,
beadwork can involve threading a few beads
together on a single string to make a simple
bracelet or necklace, or on a larger scale, to form
beaded
bags,
clothing,
or
even
wall-hangings.
Beadwork is ancient, evidenced by the findings of
beads dating back to the Stone Age. Back then,
people strung bones, shells, or rocks together to
hang around their neck. As cultures and societies
evolved over time, beadwork became a form of
personal expression, a symbol of social class, or
even a talisman to drive away bad luck.
Interestingly, some regions have particularly rich
traditions. The Ndebele tribe of South Africa,
ⓐ_______________, is famed for intricate dresses made
of glass beads. Different designs serve as a means
of marking different developmental stages of a
woman’s life. An unmarried girl may wear a square
apron onto which thousands of glass beads were
hand-sewn, while a married woman might wear a
five-paneled apron, along with beaded necklaces
and a beaded cape. ⓑ_______________, beadwork is
an essential aspect of many Native American
cultures. Beadwork powerfully expresses cultural
identity, reflecting a sense of continuity across
generations.

(A) 온라인 마케팅이 보편화됨에 따라, 인터넷과 기술은 더 널리 사용되게 되었다.(→인터넷과 기술이 더 널리 사 용됨에 따라 온라인 마케팅이 보편화되었다.) (F) (불일치) (B) 대형 브랜드들은 자사 웹사이트를 통해 자사 제품에 대한 정보를 제공해야 한다는 것을 깨달았다. (B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(businesses use)을 이끌 어 선행사 the strategies를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루 어야 하므로 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 선행사 ‘the video ~ recommendations’를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, ‘the video ~ recommendations’ 가 우리에게 ‘보여지는’ 대상이므로 수동태 are shown 이 적절하다. 11) it’s up to the consumer to decide what to believe : • ‘가주어-진주어’ 구문과 ‘up to ~(~에게 달려있는)’를 사 용하여 ‘결정하는 것은 소비자에게 달려 있다’를 단어 수 에 맞춰 영작해야 하므로, 가주어 it과 be동사 is를 축약 한 it’s를 먼저 쓰고 up to the consumer(소비자에게 달 려 있는)와 진주어 to decide를 차례대로 쓴다. • decide의 목적어인 ‘무엇을 믿을지’를 영작하기 위해 ’ 의문사+to부정사‘ 구문을 활용하여 의문사 what 뒤에 to believe를 이어 쓴다. 12) ④: ⓐ 끊임없는: 규칙적으로 또는 항상 일어나는 ⓑ ~을 유지하다: 무언가를 간직하고 있거나 계속 가지 고 있다 ⓔ 집집마다 방문하는: 한 집에서 다음 집으로 오답 ⓒ 충성도: 특히 책이나 노래가 다른 사람들에게 판매 되거나 사용될 때마다 작가나 음악가에게 지급되는 돈 (→the quality of being loyal to a particular company or brand(특정 회사나 브랜드에 대해 충성스러운 특성)) ⓓ 편의용품[시설]: 어떤 것이 하기 쉽거나 접근하기 쉽 다는 사실 (→something that is useful because it saves you time or means that you have less work to do(당신의 시간 을 절약해 주거나 당신이 해야 할 일이 줄어드는 것을 의미하기 때문에 유용한 것)) 13) ③: (A) 뒤에 동사 is가 있으므로 주어 역할을 하는 동명사 using이 적절하다. (B) 접속사 When 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 분사구 문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 many consumers가 선택에 직면한 주체이지만, 동사 face는 전치사 with와 함께 ‘be faced with ~(~에 직면하다)’의 형태로 수동태로 쓰이므로 be동사가 생략된 과거분사 구 faced with를 이루는 과거분사 faced가 적절하다. 능동 의미의 facing은 타동사로 바로 목적어를 취하므 로 뒤에 전치사 with가 올 수 없다. (C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(sparks ~ psychology)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞에 선행사 “hunger marketing”을 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 14) ②: ⓐ 앞에서 욕구를 창출하는 마케팅의 첫 번째 예로 유 명인이 특정 제품을 사용하고 팬들 또한 그 제품을 사 용함으로써 유명인과 자신을 연상시키게 하는 전략을 설명하고, 뒤에서 욕구를 창출하는 마케팅의 예로 가치 를 홍보하는 전략을 추가로 제시하고 있으므로 In addition(또한), Besides(게다가)가 적절하다. ⓑ 앞에서 브랜드들 사이에서 선택에 직면할 때 많은 소비자가 자신의 가치관과 일치하는 브랜드를 선택할 것이라고 했고, 환경적 대의를 지지하는 회사가 같은 대의를 중시하는 소비자의 관심을 더 끌 수 있다는 구 체적인 예시가 빈칸 뒤에 제시되므로 For example(예 를 들어), For instance(예를 들어)가 적절하다. 오답 ① 결과적으로 요컨대 ③ 그러므로 즉 ④ 게다가 다시 말해 ⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 예를 들어 15) ⑤: 주어진 문장은 ‘예를 들어, John이 겨울 재킷에 대한 온 라인 리뷰를 계속 읽는다면 의류 회사는 그에게 재킷 쿠폰을 보내 새로운 고객을 창출할 수 있다.’라는 의미 로, 구체적인 사례를 제시하는 문장이다. 따라서 이 문 장 앞에는 소비자의 온라인 행동을 분석하여 개인 맞춤 형 마케팅을 수행한다는 일반적인 설명이 와야 한다. (E) 앞에서 소비자의 온라인 행동 데이터를 분석함으로 써 기업이 소비자의 선호를 더 잘 이해하고 마케팅 활 동을 최적화할 수 있다는 일반적 원리를 설명하고 있으 므로 이러한 포괄적 설명 뒤에 그 원리를 실제로 보여 주는 주어진 문장이 자연스럽게 이어진다. 따라서 주어 진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다. 16) ②: 인터넷과 기술을 이용할 수 있게 되면서 마케팅이 온라 인으로 확장되었다고 언급했을 뿐, 온라인 마케팅과 오 프라인 마케팅을 비교하진 않았으므로 ② ‘비용 측면에 서 온라인 마케팅은 전통적인 오프라인 마케팅과 비교 해 얼마나 효과적인가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 무엇이 마케팅이 오프라인에서 온라인으로 확장되게 만들었는가? (→인터넷과 기술이 더 널리 이용 가능해 짐으로써) ③ 소셜 미디어 플랫폼에서 인플루언서들은 마케팅에 어떻게 기여하는가? (→인플루언서는 소셜 미디어 플랫 폼을 활용해 잠재 고객 및 커뮤니티와 소통함으로써 마 케팅에 기여한다.) ④ 타깃 시청자의 측면에서 스트리밍 서비스는 방송 텔 레비전과 어떻게 다른가? (→스트리밍 서비스는 방송 텔레비전보다 더 특정한 시청자와 연결할 수 있다.) ⑤ 온라인 연결의 부수적인 이점은 무엇이며, 기업들은 그것을 어떻게 활용하는가? (→부수적인 이점은 데이터 이며, 기업들은 소비자의 온라인 행동 데이터를 분석하 여 소비자 선호를 더 잘 이해하고 마케팅 전략을 최적 화한다.) 17) needs, trust, personalized, feedback 요약문 기업들이 다양한 소비자 요구를 충족시키려고 노력 함에 따라, 그들은 개인화된 경험을 제공함으로써 소비자들 과의 신뢰를 구축하기 위해 밈 마케팅을 사용하고, 한편 인 플루언서 마케팅은 소비자들이 원하는 것에 대한 피드백을 얻는 데 도움을 준다. 18) ④: 지문 앞부분에서 특정 브랜드의 사용이 곧 '지위의 상 징'이라고 언급했으므로 유명인이 특정 제품의 홍보대 사로 나설 때, 팬들은 그 제품을 사용함으로써 자신과 유명인을 연결 짓게 되고, 결과적으로 소비자들은 제품 사용을 통해 해당 유명인과 유사한 지위를 공유한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ④ ‘인기 있는 유명인과 자신을 연상시킬 수 있다 ‘이다. 오답 ① 자신이 좋아하는 유명인들과 직접 소통할 수 있다 ② 브랜드와는 별개로 자신만의 고유한 정체성을 강화 한다 ③ 제품의 환경적 영향에 대해 비판적으로 되다 ⑤ 제품의 실용적인 기능에 집중한다

rescuing a koala ⓐwas captured. Here in the
studio is Karen, the wildlife ranger.
W: Thanks for having me.

W: There was a forest fire, so I went to rescue
animals ⓒneeded help. I saw a koala near the
flame.
M: So, you rushed to save it?
W: Yes. I immediately ran and ⓓgrabbed it.
M: And you covered it with a blanket. Why did you
do that?
W: (A)It’s necessary to cover frightened animals for
safety. It reduces their stress and prevents them
from biting or scratching.

name, Joy!
M: ⓔWhat a perfect name! Thank you for showing

It is vital to cover frightened animals for safety.

solution: 밑줄 친 (A)는 ‘It’s necessary to ~(~하는 것이 필요하다)‘를 사 용하여 ’안전을 위해 겁먹은 동물들을 덮어주는 것이 필요합니 다.‘라는 의무를 표현하고 있으므로, 금지를 나타내는 ❺ ’안전 을 위해 겁먹은 동물들을 덮어주는 것은 금지됩니다.‘와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

Nairobi, Kenya is unique because it is the world’s
only capital with a national park, which ⓐattracts
many international tourists with wild lions and other
beasts against the backdrop of tall buildings in its
urban center. Living near the park, a thirteen-year-old
boy named Richard Turere was responsible for
keeping his family’s cattle safe from lions that often
came out of the park at night to hunt. Many
neighbors had lost their cows, and others their
goats and sheep.
While ⓑrounding up his cattle one night, Richard
discovered that lions were scared of moving lights
and didn’t come near the cattle enclosure when he
walked around carrying a flashlight. Soon, he
fastened flashing LED bulbs onto poles around the
enclosure facing the outside and connected (A)them
to an old car battery powered by a solar panel. He
devised the lights to ⓒflicker on and off from time
to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed his
first “lion lights,” he never spotted lions again, and
his family didn’t lose any cattle to (B)them. Neighbors
ⓓfollowed suit, protecting their valuable source of
income without killing (C)the unwanted neighbors.
This is an example of a keen observation on animal
behavior leading to a creative ⓔapproach that
brought peace and harmony.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ attract: to make someone or something comesomewhere or take part in something
ⓑ round ~ up: to force someone or somethingto leave
ⓒ flicker: (of a light or a flame) to keep goingon and off as it shines or burns
ⓓ follow suit: to do the same as someone elsehas done
ⓔ approach: a method of doing something ordealing with a problem
solution: ⓑ ‘round ~ up’은 ‘~을 모아들이다’라는 뜻이나 ‘to force someone or something to leave(누군가나 어떤 것을 강제로 떠나게 하다)’는 ‘drive ~ out(~을 쫓아내다[내몰다])’과 같은 표현에 대한 설명이므로, ‘to find and gather together a group of people, animals, or things(한 무리의 사람들, 동물들이나 사물들을 찾아서 모으다)’와 같은 설명으로 고쳐야 한다.

Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent
studies,
(A)_____________,
reveal
there’s
another aspect to this story. It turns out that wild
animals, those that haven’t been specifically bred to
live with humans, are also willing to form mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
them
to
communicate that they will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
(B)_____________, the fishers catch much more fish,
and the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to
escape from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that
engage in this fishing are more likely to live longer,
by 13 percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins
may end up swimming to areas where there aren’t
many fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal
fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

million
squirrels
were
living
in
Chicago
and
approximately 10,000 foxes in London. In Seoul, 155
wild boars were captured in 2022. Why are there so
many animals in big cities? (A) One reason is that
many cities are built on biologically fertile and
productive land areas, which are attractive not only
to humans but to other creatures as well. (B)
Another reason is due to urban areas becoming
greener, inviting more wild animals. (C) In addition,
for some animal species, cities have become a
perfect place for feeding, mating, and nesting. (D)
Peregrine falcons, for example, use tall buildings for
nesting sites, man-made lighting to hunt for prey at
night, and warm urban air currents to soar easily.
(E) Cities have become home, sweet home, not only
to humans but to wild animals.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Cities have become attractive places to live notonly for humans but also for animals.
Urban wildlife problems mainly result from poorwaste management and careless human behavior.
Green city projects are designed primarily forhuman recreation rather than for wildlife survival.
Predators living in cities pose serious dangersthat make urban environments unsafe for residents.
The presence of wild animals in cities requiresstrict human control and population management.

다음 주어진 대화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

M: Hey, Kelly. Look at the picture of a bird. What
do you think it’s eating?
W: Oh, that’s a honeyguide bird. It’s eating some
bits of the bee nest.
(A) M: Fascinating! What happens next?
W: Once they find the nest, the humans use
smoke to drive the bees away and collect
the honey.
(B) M: How can it do that without getting attacked
by bees?
W: Well, the bees are not there due to some
help from humans.
(C) M: Ah, so that’s when the birds can access the
food without getting attacked.
W: Yes. It’s a beautiful partnership between
birds and humans!
(D) M: Really? Can you explain how that works?
W: Well, when a honeyguide bird sees humans
in the forest, it makes a loud noise and
guides them to bee nests.
solution: 사진을 보며 꿀잡이새가 벌집의 일부분을 먹고 있다고 말하는 주어진 대화에 이어, 대명사 that으로 그 동작을 가리켜 벌의 공격을 받지 않고 먹을 수 있는 이유에 대해 궁금해 하자 인 간의 도움으로 거기에 벌들이 없다고 답하는 (B), 대명사 that 으로 인간의 도움으로 벌이 없는 것을 가리켜 어떻게 그렇게 되는지 설명해 달라고 요청하고, 꿀잡이새가 인간들을 발견하 면 큰 소리를 내어 그들을 벌집으로 안내한다고 설명하는 (D), 그런 다음에 어떤 일이 일어나는지 궁금해 하고, 인간들이 연 기를 이용해 벌을 내쫓고 꿀을 채집한다고 설명하는 (A), 접속 사 so(그래서)로 결과를 연결하고 대명사 that으로 인간들이 연기로 벌을 내쫓고 꿀을 채집한 것을 가리켜 그때 새들이 공 격받지 않고 먹이에 접근할 수 있다고 한 뒤 새들과 인간의 아름다운 파트너십이라고 마무리짓는 (C)로 이어지는 것이 적 절하다.

Coyotes and racoons cause conflicts with residents
in many towns in North America. Elephants damage
crops and property in Africa. Wild boars destroy
agricultural fields in Asia and Europe. The idea
(A)[of / that] wild animals are annoyances or threats
that need to be eliminated is common in many
parts of the world. However, often, unintended
consequences occur because of this attitude. A
balanced approach is needed, particularly between
human safety and the well-being of the animals,
(B)[which / where] can be found when we grasp a
proper understanding of their behavior as well as
their role in their natural habitat. After all, we
should acknowledge the fact that both humans and
animals are temporary tenants of this precious
planet. Neither is less valuable nor more valuable
than (C)[another / the other]. Maintaining balance
and harmony among all living species is the only
choice.
(A)
(B)
(C)

(B) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ habitat)을 이끌어 주어인 명사구 A balanced approach를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 참고로, 관계부사 where 뒤에는 완전한 절 이 이어져야 한다. (C) 주어에 부정대명사로 쓰인 Neither(둘 중 어느 쪽도 아닌) 의 비교 대상에는 ‘(둘 중) 나머지 다른 하나’를 뜻하여 부정대 명사로 쓰인 the other가 적절하다. 참고로, 언급된 대상에 추 가하여 더 존재하는 상황에서 ‘(추가로) 또 다른 하나’를 뜻하 는 경우 another를 부정대명사로 쓴다. 비상(홍민표) 3과

Nairobi, Kenya is unique because it is the world’s
only capital with a national park, which attracts

urban

near

park,
a

to time. It worked perfectly. After he installed his

Unexpected Neighbors
In a suburb in the Pacific Northwest, Justin ties his
shoes for his morning run and steps out at dawn.
As he walks off his front step, he spots some
racoons crossing the street. Up in a tree, he sees a
family of squirrels. Birds begin to sing, and he
enjoys the beauty of his neighborhood. While
running, a dangerous sight interrupts the idyllic
scene. A coyote watches as a black bear searches
through a garbage bin for food. Justin is surprised
at his neighborhood transforming into a place full
of wildlife encounters.
Why Animals Migrate to Cities
In 2019, it was estimated that more than 1.5
million
squirrels
were
living
in
Chicago
and
approximately 10,000 foxes in London. In Seoul, 155
wild boars were captured in 2022. Why are there so
many animals in big cities? One reason is that
many cities are built on biologically fertile and
productive land areas, which are attractive not only
to humans but to other creatures as well. Another
reason is due to _______________________________________
___________________________. Cities have begun building
more gardens, parks, and legally protected areas for
educational,
recreational,
or
other
purposes,
attracting more wild creatures. In addition, for some
animal species, cities have become a perfect place
for feeding, mating, and nesting. Peregrine falcons,
for example, use tall buildings for nesting sites,
man-made lighting to hunt for prey at night, and
warm urban air currents to soar easily. Cities have
become home, sweet home, not only to humans
but to wild animals.
To some, living among animals might sound idyllic,
but to others, wild animals near residential areas,
especially those predators high up in the food
chain, can be an annoyance and a threat. What
could be an optimal approach to dealing with these
new neighbors? Is there a solution for humans and
animals to live together peacefully in their shared
habitat?

choices: urban areas becoming smaller, limiting animalhabitats
rural areas becoming greener, attracting animalsout of cities
urban areas becoming greener, inviting morewild animals
urban areas becoming noisier, driving wildanimals away
natural areas becoming protected, reducinganimal movement

In
1981,
tragic
news
shocked
Los
Angeles
residents. A three-year-old girl was attacked and
killed by a coyote in front of her home. People
were outraged and immediately took action to
remove the species from their neighborhoods. They
killed a total of 55 coyotes over a period of 80
days.
Scientists,
however,
questioned
such
a
destructive control method, as coyotes are highly
adaptive and breed quickly. A study showed that a
simulated coyote population survived indefinitely
when 70% were killed annually. This means that
killing even most of the coyotes in a population
will have no significant effect. In coyote packs, a
dominant adult pair maintains a strict structure that
prevents others from breeding and controls the
population.
Destructive
control
methods
often
disrupt this social structure, resulting in increased
populations. Moreover, completely eliminating the
species using a control method could cause other
issues such as over-population of rodents and other
small prey. Clearly, (A)it is difficult to predict how
nature will balance itself out when humans attempt
to control.

Nature always returns to balance when humansapply strict control methods.
Human control over nature usually producesclear and predictable results.
Nature can be fully managed if humansunderstand ecological systems well enough.
Nature does not follow human intentions, andhasty control may lead to unexpected outcomes.

body:
Throughout history, humans and animals have
worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped
round up sheep, horses and cows helped with
farming, and some animals assisted with hunting
and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has
always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there’s another
aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals,
those that haven’t been specifically bred to live with
humans,
are
also
willing
to
form
mutual
relationships with humans. One outstanding example
is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have
teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used
drones and underwater cameras to observe this
unique
partnership.
When
migrating
mullets
approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins
drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand
ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers
watch
the
dolphins,
looking
for
them
to
communicate that they will be making a “deep
dive,” which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then
cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets
towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and
the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape
from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in
this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13
percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end
up swimming to areas where there aren’t many fish,
and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins
and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way
to catch fish. It’s a win-win for both humans and
animals, a reminder of how our interactions and
relationships with the natural world can be mutually
beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive
for generations, and it continues to inspire us
today.

How Modern Technology Has Completely ChangedTraditional Fishing Methods
The History of Animal Domestication and ItsImportance in Human Society
Scientific Research Proving That Dolphins AreMore Intelligent than Other Animals
A Win-win Partnership Between Dolphins and Fishersin Laguna Showing Human-Nature Coexistence

농업 관행 ② 야생 포식자를 통제하기 위해 설계된 정부 주도의 보존 프로그램 ③ 전문적인 관리를 필요로 하는 값비싼 기술 시스템 ⑤ 동물들이 인간의 활동에 익숙해지자 실패한 일시적 인 방법 13) ③: 대도시에 동물들이 많은 첫 번째 이유로 도시가 건설되 는 지역의 생물학적 이점을 설명한 뒤에 또 다른 이유 로 제시되고 있으며, 도시들이 다양한 목적을 위해 더 많은 정원, 공원들과 법적인 보호 구역을 건설하기 시 작했고 이것이 더 많은 야생 동물을 유인했다는 구체적 인 설명이 뒤에 이어지므로, 도시 지역에 녹지 공간들 이 많아지면서 야생 동물들을 끌어들인다는 흐름으로 빈칸에는 ③ ‘도시 지역들이 더 푸르게 되면서 더 많은 야생 동물들을 유인하는 것’이 적절하다. 오답 ① 도시 지역이 더 작아지면서 동물의 서식지를 제한하 는 것 ② 시골 지역이 더 푸르게 되면서 동물들을 도시 밖으 로 이끄는 것 ④ 도시 지역이 더 시끄러워지면서 야생 동물을 쫓아내 는 것 ⑤ 자연 지역이 보호되어 동물들의 이동을 감소시키는 것 14) ③: 차례대로 T-F-T-F-T이다. (A) Justin의 동네는 목가적인 분위기를 만드는 다람쥐 나 새들과 같은 야생 동물들이 있지만, 흑곰들과 같은 위험한 동물들도 있다. (T) (B) 시카고, 런던, 서울과 같은 대도시에서 야생 동물들 의 수는 눈에 띄게 감소했다. (→ 2019년에는 시카고에 150만 마리 이상의 다람쥐가, 런던에는 약 1만 마리의 여우가 살고 있는 것으로 추정되었으며, 서울에서는 2022년에 155마리의 멧돼지가 포획되었다.) (F) (C) 많은 야생 동물들이 비옥하고 생산성 있는 토지를 찾아 대도시로 온다. (T) (D) 대도시들은 야생 동물들의 생활 터전을 확보하기 위해 정원, 공원, 법적인 보호 구역들을 늘리고 있다. (→ 도시들은 교육, 오락 또는 다른 목적을 위해 더 많 은 정원, 공원, 그리고 법적인 보호 구역을 건설하기 시 작했으며, 이것이 더 많은 야생 동물들을 유인했다.) (F) (E) 야생 동물들과 도시에서 함께 살아가는 것에 대해 사람들은 엇갈리는 의견들을 가지고 있다. (T) 15) ⑤: 코요테를 죽이는 파괴적인 통제 방법은 번식을 통제하 는 코요테 무리의 엄격한 사회 구조를 붕괴시켜 개체 수 증가를 야기하고, 설치류나 다른 피식 동물의 과잉 과 같은 다른 문제들도 야기할 수 있다고 했으므로, 자 연은 인간의 예상대로 작용하지 않으며, 인간의 통제는 의도와는 다른 결과를 낳고 오히려 생태계의 균형을 무너뜨릴 수도 있다는 결론을 도출할 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 (A) ‘인간이 통제를 시도할 때 자연이 어떻게 균형을 이룰지 예측하는 것은 어렵다’가 의미하는 바로 ⑤ ‘자연은 인간의 의도를 따르지 않으며, 성급한 통제 는 예상치 못한 결과로 이어질 수 있다.’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 신중한 인간의 계획은 자연의 균형을 통제하는 것 을 쉽게 만든다. ② 인간이 엄격한 통제 방법을 적용할 때 자연은 항상 균형 상태로 되돌아간다. ③ 자연에 대한 인간의 통제는 보통 명확하고 예측 가 능한 결과를 낳는다. ④ 인간이 생태계를 충분히 잘 이해한다면 자연은 완 전히 관리될 수 있다. 16) ③: 어린 소녀가 자택 앞에서 코요테에게 공격을 당해 죽은 비극적인 사건 이후 사람들이 코요테 종을 제거하기 위 해 많은 코요테를 죽였지만 큰 효과가 없었으며, 그 이 유에 대해 이러한 파괴적인 통제 방법은 코요테 무리의 사회 구조를 붕괴시켜 개체 수 증가를 야기하고, 설치 류나 다른 피식 동물의 개체 수 과잉과 같은 다른 문제 들도 야기할 수 있다고 설명하는 내용이므로, 글의 제 목으로 ③ ‘코요테를 죽여 개체 수를 통제하려는 시도 가 결국 실패한 이유’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 코요테는 어떻게 도시의 지역에서 가장 위험한 포식 자가 되었는가 ② 도시에서 야생 동물들에 대한 인간의 두려움과 폭력 적 대응의 역사 ④ 과학자들과 지방 정부에 의해 개발된 성공적인 야생 동물 통제 방법 ⑤ 코요테를 제거하는 것이 도시의 설치류 개체 수에 미치는 즉각적인 그리고 장기적인 영향 17) Balanced, Humans, Wild Animals 제시문 인간들과 야생 동물들 사이의 평화로운 공존에 대 한 균형 잡힌 시각의 필요성 18) ⑤: 인간과 야생 동물들의 상호 관계를 형성한 사례 중 하 나로 브라질의 라구나에 있는 돌고래와 어부들의 130 년 이상의 물고기를 잡기 위한 협력에 대해 소개하며, 이는 인간과 자연과의 상호 작용 및 관계가 어떻게 서 로에게 이로울 수 있는지를 상기시켜 주는 사례라고 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ⑤ ‘인간-자연의 상 생을 보여주는 라구나의 돌고래들과 어부들 간의 서로 에게 도움이 되는 협력 관계’가 적절하다. 오답 ① 브라질 해안가 지역의 어부들과 야생 돌고래 사이 의 갈등 ② 현대 기술이 전통적인 어업 방식에 완전히 변화를 가져온 방식 ③ 동물의 가축화의 역사와 인간 사회에서 그것의 중 요성 ④ 돌고래가 다른 동물들보다 더 지능적이라는 것을 입증하는 과학적 연구 19) ②: ‘그러나 이러한 태도 때문에 종종 의도치 않은 결과가 발생한다.’라는 역접의 연결어 However(하지만)에 의해 부정적으로 전환된 뜻의 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 태도 (this attitude)’가 가리키는 내용, 즉 야생 동물들이 제 거되어야 할 골칫거리나 위협이라는 생각이 세계 여러 지역에서 흔하다고 언급하는 문장 뒤이자, 의도치 않은 결과가 발생할 수 있는 문제점에 대해 인간의 안전과 동물의 복지 사이에서 균형 잡힌 접근법이 필요하다는 해결책을 제시하는 문장 앞인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 적 절하다. 20) ③: 요약문 코요테 한 마리가 주거 지역에서 어린 아이를 죽인 비극적인 사건 이후, 사람들은 그 종을 (A)제거하 려고 시도했으나, 이러한 파괴적인 통제 방법은 코요테 무리의 사회적인 구조를 파괴하여 개체 수를 (B)늘리고 심지어 추가적인 부작용들도 야기한다. 오답 ① 제거하다 줄이는 ② 기르다, 사육하다 줄이는 ④ 먹이를 주다 안정시키는 ⑤ 훈련시키다 증가시키는

ⓐ[is / are] able to track and record fish behavior
better than humans can, especially when the system
is trained with enough relevant data. It can
distinguish and identify one fish from another and
diagnose whether a small speck is dirt or sea lice,
and this information is entered into the fish’s health
record. In a sense, the fish farm (A)__________________
__________________________________________________________
______________. Farmers can then determine when
they should take action, such as when to separate
an abnormal group from the rest or spread out the
fish population to reduce density, without resorting
to harsh chemical treatments, ⓑ[in which / which]
can harm the fish, the environment, and even the
consumer. In addition, all this data from cameras
and sensors can ⓒ[utilize / be utilized] for various
applications and purposes.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ
ⓑ

solution: ⓐ 주어가 전치사구(with ~ capabilities)의 수식을 받는 단수명사 구 A computer system이므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 is가 알맞다. ⓑ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ consumer) 을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 harsh chemical treatments를 부연 설 명하는 관계사절을 이루므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 뒤에는 완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. ⓒ 조동사 can에 연결되는 동사원형이 올 자리이며, 주어 all this data from cameras and sensors가 타동사 utilize(~을 활 용하다)의 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 수동태 be utilized가 알맞다.

body:
AI continues to advance in aquaculture to extend
beyond caged fish.
(A) Swarm robots, or many small robots working
together, can swim in and around seaweed
farms to collect data and then make decisions
on how to deal with problems that arise. Single
larger robots or even humans may be available
to take care of the physical labor from
removing harmful weeds to harvesting; however,
swarm robots may be more efficient and
cost-effective.
(B) In particular, smart fish farming technologies can
be applied to seaweed farming. Seaweed is as
ⓐ[a valuable source / valuable a source] of
food as fish. It’s also a source of fuel and an
important ingredient for cosmetics, fertilizers,
and other medicinal and industrial products.
(C) As such, ongoing research is exploring various ways
ⓑ[which / that] AI can help in the seaweed
industry, including the use of autonomous
underwater vehicles (AUVs) and swarm robotics.
Using cameras and sensors, AUVs can do many
of
the
analytical
and
diagnostic
tasks
on
seaweed farms.
The potential of AI in aquaculture is vast, and it
brings a more sustainable and technologically driven
future for fish and seaweed farming. Families that
gather together, eagerly ⓒ[anticipate / anticipating]
a healthy seafood dinner, may not be aware of the
carefully monitored fish and seaweed farms or the
cutting-edge AI technology involved in getting food
to their table. However, the process of doing so is
evidence of the considerable amount of investment
in sustainable, high-quality aquaculture with AI.
㉠With AI as an ally, the future of the oceans and
the nourishment of humanity is just a little bit more
secure.

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I ⓐgive advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? In fact, most
people believe they make a worse impression than
they
actually
do.
Researchers
performed
an
experiment where students were ⓑpaired up for
five-minute ice breaking conversations. They were
then asked to rate how much they liked their
partners. Additionally, researchers asked participants
if they thought their partners liked them. Most
participants’ estimations of their partners’ responses
were pessimistic, which were ⓒidentical to the real
responses. It turns out that participants do not
make bad impressions but make better impressions
than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
ⓓmismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
In other words, our ⓔflexible attitudes may prevent
us from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry
about the impression you think you make on
people; chances are you can be confident that the
impression you make is just ⓕfine.

다음 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?

The second point I want to make today is about
thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people
believe that their personality falls into a specific
category and often blame their weaknesses or
failures on their personality type.
(A) If you choose to behave differently and make
needed changes, your personality will also
change. People are predictable and consistent
over time only because they choose to be, so
don’t limit yourself to a certain type. Start
crafting the person you want to become today.
(B) Who was your favorite singer? What did you
hope to become when you grow up? Do you
feel the same way now? What will your answers
be 10 years from now? I bet you don’t know.
Just like your likes and future dreams keep
changing, so do you.
(C) For example, they may say they can’t do
something because they aren’t that kind of
person. However, personality categorizations are
neither
absolute
nor
permanent.
Try
to
remember yourself from ten years ago.

body:
During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman
with a brightly decorated prosthetic leg proudly
walked the runway at a major fashion show. She
was Mama Cax, a model and influencer.
Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost
her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was
depressed and struggled to accept her new body.
However, with the support of her family and
friends, Cax learned to love it. One day when she
was 26, Cax posted a picture on social media
showing her leg. “I didn’t think it could help
anyone,” she said in an interview, “But after
receiving messages of support, I realized my story
could inspire others.” After receiving support from
others, she began to use social media to share
more about her life and to inspire others. She
proudly posted pictures of herself wearing stylish
prosthetic covers and spoke out about body
positivity and fashion. In 2016, she became the first
model for the #RunwayForAll campaign. In 2018,
she appeared on the cover of major fashion
magazines.
When asked, “How did you come to embrace
yourself?” she replied, “The truth is, like many
people, I’m still on my journey to self-love. There
are many barriers ahead.” In addition to modeling,
Cax showed her ability to overcome physical
barriers
by
swimming,
playing
basketball,
and
mountain climbing. She even finished the New York
City Marathon in a wheelchair.
Sadly, Mama Cax’s journey was cut short in 2019.
Although she is no longer with us, her journey will
remain in our hearts, inspiring us to (A)______________
__________________________________________________________.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: develop strengths in various fields
create healthier habits to maintain physical health
pay more attention to and respect people withdisabilities
overcome limitations and find our own paths tosuccess and happiness
dress appropriately and act in a proper mannerto make good impressions on others
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

London Transport Workers Study
In the busy London streets of 1953, a special study
was conducted. Scientists observed more than 31,000
people who had various jobs on buses and trains.
Some jobs demanded lots of moving around, like
ticket collectors, while others, like drivers, didn’t
require much movement. What was interesting was
that the workers with more active jobs had fewer
heart problems than those who sat a lot. This implied
that jobs requiring more moving around were healthier
for workers than those jobs that didn’t. What could
account for the difference in their health outcomes?

Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or ⓐfixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain ⓑworking; this is called the basal
metabolic rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%,
is used to consume and ⓒabsorbs energy from
food and is called the thermic effect of food (TEF).
In short, BMR and TEF are the minimum energy
ⓓrequired for the body to stay alive. The remaining
400 calories, or 20%, is used for things people
choose to do, including various physical activities
(PA) like working, playing, and moving around.
Maybe some of the London public transportation
workers
spent
the
remaining
20%
differently,
ⓔresulted in their different health outcomes.

(A) About seventy percent of daily energy is used
to keep the body’s vital organs functioning. (T/F)
(B) The thermic effect of food refers to the energy
spent digesting and absorbing nutrients. (T/F)
(C) Basal metabolic rate and TEF together represent
the minimum energy for survival. (T/F)
(D) The amount of energy consumed for our physical
activities is about 10 percent. (T/F)
(E) Differences in how people used their remaining
energy may have influenced their health results. (T/F)

(T) (일치) (D) 우리의 신체 활동으로 소비되는 에너지의 양은 약 10(→ 20)퍼센트이다. (F) (불일치) (E) 남은 에너지를 어떻게 사용했는지의 차이가 그들의 건강 결과에 영향을 미쳤을지도 모른다. (T) (일치)

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym,
playing badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a
hike. (A)____________, those calories may also be
burned by small, seemingly unimportant activities
we do throughout the day, like standing up and
sitting down, walking around the house, washing
dishes, doing the laundry, taking out the garbage,
and many others. These actions are collectively
called Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis (NEAT)
as they use up energy too! (B)____________, a
40-minute run will burn around 400 calories. Doing
this could use up the excess energy budget
completely, but not everyone has 40 minutes a day
to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps, which is like
walking about 8 kilometers, burns 400 calories as
well. What this means is that while a 40-minute run
will burn 400 calories, doing small things like more
walking, taking stairs, or even just cleaning your
room can add up at the end of the day, too.
