grams of fat. This is not healthy over the long
term. While NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and
muscles with the same benefits that exercise does,
excess energy still gets used up instead of being
(A)[released / stored]. You may not necessarily get
fit, but you’ll stay in energy balance, which is
important for long term health.
Further Health Benefits
Paying attention to NEAT has other health benefits
as well. Sitting too much can cause problems like
heart disease and muscle loss, so standing not only
increases NEAT but also decreases sitting time,
which is a win-win. As people get older, it may
become more difficult to stay healthy, so adopting
a lifestyle that (B)[increases / decreases] NEAT is a
good habit for younger people to make. Walking
more, taking stairs, or even using smaller water
cups so they have to be refilled more often
(C)[accumulates / uses] energy. Whether it’s for
weight management or trying to stay more active
during exam week, understanding NEAT is a great
way to maintain energy balance in the body.
(A)
(B)
(C)

The answer to this requires a simple formula and
a little bit of math. The formula is an easy
equation: the total energy expenditure of the body
equals 「BMR + TEF + PA」. In the human body, the
energy from different foods people eat is used to
keep
everything
running
smoothly.
The
basal
metabolic rate (BMR) is a measurement of how
much energy is needed to stay alive; the thermic
effect of food (TEF) is a measurement of the energy
used to consume and absorb energy from food;
and physical activity (PA) is a measurement of the
energy (A)[using / used] beyond just lying in bed.
Learning about the composition of these three
elements can help people make better choices for
their health and well-being.
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000 calories,
about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to essential
functions such as keeping the heart and the brain
(B)[to work / working]; this is called the basal
metabolic rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is
used to consume and absorb energy from food and
is called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for
the body (C)[stays / to stay] alive. The remaining 400
calories, or 20%, is used for things people choose to
do, including various physical activities (PA) like
working, playing, and moving around. Maybe some
of the London public transportation workers spent
the remaining 20% differently, resulting in their
different health outcomes.

다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?

In the busy London streets of 1953, a special
study was conducted. Scientists observed more than
31,000 people who had various jobs on buses and
trains. Some jobs demanded lots of moving around,
like ticket collectors, while others, like drivers, didn’t
require much movement. What was interesting was
that the workers with more active jobs had fewer
heart problems than those who sat a lot. This
implied that jobs requiring more moving around
were healthier for workers than those jobs that
didn’t. What could account for the difference in
their health outcomes?
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000 calories,
about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to essential
functions such as keeping the heart and the brain
working; this is called the basal metabolic rate (BMR).
Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to consume and
absorb energy from food and is called the thermic
effect of food (TEF). In short, BMR and TEF are the
minimum energy required for the body to stay alive.
The remaining 400 calories, or 20%, is used for
things people choose to do, including various
physical activities (PA) like working, playing, and
moving around. Maybe some of the London public
transportation workers spent the remaining 20%
differently, resulting in their different health outcomes.
choices: Since BMR accounts for the largest portion oftotal energy expenditure, differences in BMRmay lead to different health outcomes.
How the remaining energy is used for physicalactivity explains the health differences amongLondon transport workers.
Increasing the thermic effect of food (TEF) is moreeffective for health than increasing physical activity.
The portion of energy used for physical activity remainsconstant regardless of occupation or environment.
Reducing daily calorie intake can prevent healthissues even with decreased physical activity.

In the big picture, your body is like an energy

(B) keeping의 목적어 the heart and the brain에 이어 지는 목적격 보어자리로, keep은 ‘keep+목적어+-ing(… 가 계속 ~하게 하다)’의 5형식 구조로 쓰이므로 현재분 사 working은 적절하다. (C) 앞에 의미상 주어 for the body가 있으므로 to stay가 적절하다. 12) BMR, TEF, fixed[set], health outcomes 요약문 신체의 총에너지 소비는 BMR, TEF, 그리고 PA로 구성되며, 80%를 차지하는 BMR과 TEF는 대부분 고정되어 [정해져] 있는 반면, 사람들이 남은 20%를 어떻게 사용하는 지의 차이가 그들의 건강 결과에 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 13) ④: 주어진 문장은 ‘이는 더 많이 움직여야 하는 직업이 그 렇지 않은 직업보다 근로자의 건강에 더 좋다는 것을 암시했다.’라는 뜻으로 이 문장 앞에는 더 많이 움직이 는 그룹이 그렇지 않은 그룹보다 건강 지표가 더 좋게 나타났다는 내용이 와야 한다. (D) 앞에서 활동적인 노 동자들이 심장 문제가 더 적었다는 연구 결과가 제시되 었고, 이것을 주어진 문장에서 This로 이어받아 움직이 는 직업이 더 건강하다는 결론을 제시하고 있으므로 주 어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (D)이다. 14) ①: 운동만큼의 강도는 아니더라도, 일상 속 사소한 움직임 인 NEAT를 누적하는 것은 운동에 버금가는 에너지를 소비함으로써 신체의 에너지 균형과 장기적인 건강을 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 것이 핵심 내용이므 로 ① ‘NEAT를 축적하는 것이 일일 에너지 소비와 균 형에 미치는 중요한 영향’이다. 오답 ② 칼로리를 소모하는 것만으로는 체중을 감량하기가 어 려운 이유 ③ 지방 감소를 위한 NEAT와 고강도 운동 사이의 비교 ④ 에너지 균형을 위해 당신의 일일 칼로리 섭취를 줄이 는 방법 ⑤ 왜 당신의 몸이 과잉 에너지를 지방으로 저장하는지 15) ②: (A) 앞에서 하루 종일 먹고 움직이지 않으면 신체는 400칼로리를 44g의 지방으로 전환할 수 있다고 했고, NEAT를 통해서 과잉 에너지는 ‘저장되는’ 대신에 소모 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 stored(저장된)가 적절하다. released 방출된 (B) 앞에서 NEAT에 주의를 기울이면 다른 건강상의 이 점도 있다고 했으므로 NEAT를 ‘늘리는’ 생활 방식을 택하는 것이 좋은 습관이 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 increases(늘리다)가 적절하다. decrease 줄이다 (C) NEAT는 에너지를 소모하는 행위이므로 더 많이 걷기, 계단 이용하기, 물 컵을 더 자주 채우기 위해 더 작은 물 컵 사용하기 등은 모두 에너지를 ‘사용한다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 uses(사용하다)가 적절하다. accumulate 축적하다 16) ②: 런던 교통 근로자들을 대상으로 한 연구에서, 많이 움 직여야 하는 직업을 가진 근로자들이 오래 앉아 있는 직업을 가진 근로자들보다 심장 질환이 적었다는 사실 이 밝혀졌고, 그 이유를 총에너지 소비량 구조에서 찾 고 있다. 전체 에너지 중 BMR과 TEF처럼 생존에 필요 한 고정된 에너지를 제외하면 약 20%가 개인의 신체 활동에 사용되는데, 이 남은 에너지를 어떻게 활용하느 냐에 따라 건강 결과가 달라질 수 있다는 내용의 글이 므로, 이 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은 ② ‘신체 활동 을 위해 남는 에너지를 어떻게 사용하는지가 런던 교 통 근로자들의 건강 차이를 설명한다.’이다. 오답 ① BMR이 총에너지 소비에서 가장 큰 비중을 차지하 므로, BMR의 차이가 서로 다른 건강 결과를 초래할 수 있다. ③ 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)를 증가시키는 것이 신체 활 동을 증가시키는 것보다 건강에 더 효과적이다. ④ 신체 활동에 사용되는 에너지의 비중은 직업이나 환경과 관계없이 일정하게 유지된다. ⑤ 신체 활동이 감소하더라도 일일 칼로리 섭취를 줄 이면 건강 문제를 예방할 수 있다. 17) ②: ⓑ burning → burns (주어인 동명사구 Taking 10,000 steps를 부연 설명하는 관계사절(which ~ 8 kilometers) 이 이중 콤마(,)로 주어와 동사 사이에 삽입된 형태로, 문장의 동사 자리이다. 따라서 주어인 동명사구는 단수 취급하므로 이에 수일치하도록 burning을 단수동사 burns로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ the day)을 이끌 어 선행사 small, seemingly unimportant activities를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 목적격 관계대 명사 that은 적절하다. *ⓐ는 목적격 관계대명사로 원래 지문에서 생략되었음 ⓒ 완전한 절(while ~ too)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어 지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다. ⓓ 전치사구 instead of에 이어지는 목적어 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 excess energy가 ‘저장되는’ 대상이므로 동명사의 수동태(being+p.p.) being stored는 적절하다. ⓔ 콤마(,) 앞에 절(you’ll ~  balance)을 선행사로 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 절 전체가 선행사일 때 단수 취급하므로 단수도 수일치한 단수동사 is는 적 절하다. 18) ④: (A) 신체는 균형을 유지할 필요가 있는 에너지 장부책 과 같다고 했고, 섭취하는 모든 음식이 장부 속 수입이 라고 했으므로 균형을 유지하기 위해 에너지를 ‘소비 해’야 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어 갈 말로 적절한 것은 expend(소비하다), consume(소모 하다), spend(소비하다)이다. (B) 앞에서 과잉 에너지를 사용하지 않고 너무 많은 음 식을 섭취하면 신체는 그 추가분을 지방으로 저장하게 된다고 했으므로 이것이 ‘건강에 좋지’ 않다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 sound(건강한), healthy(건강한), good(좋은)이다. 오답 ① 아끼다 건강한 ② 소비하다 건강하지 못한 ③ 소모하다 해로운 ⑤ 보존하다 좋은

위 대화의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)                      (B)
choices: SoIn short
HoweverIn brief
ThereforeTo illustrate this point
NonethelessTo give you an example
For exampleOn the contrary
solution: (A) 자신은 컴퓨터 게임에 관심이 있고 상당히 창의적이라는 앞 내용을 이유로 컴퓨터 게임 회사를 시작하는 것을 고려중 이라는 결론을 연결하므로, 빈칸에는 So(그래서)나 Therefore (그러므로, 따라서)가 적절하다. (B) 다양한 과목을 공부함으로써 영감을 얻을 수 있다는 앞 내 용에 대한 구체적 예시로 많은 컴퓨터 업계 최고 경영자들은 자신들이 수강했던 철학, 심리학, 또는 역사학 과정이 다양한 방식으로 그들에게 영감을 주었다고 말한다는 내용을 연결하 고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 To illustrate this point(이 요점을 예를 들어 설명하자면) 또는 To give you an example(예시를 하나 들자면)이 적절하다.

body:
Hello,
everyone!
Thank
you
for
your
warm
welcome. (A)고향 같은 곳에 돌아와서 좋지만 오늘은
공연을 하러가 아니라 뮤지션으로서의 제 삶에 대해
이야기하려고 여러분을 방문했습니다. Last year, after
20 years of hard work, I finally signed my first
record company contract. I’d like to tell you a
hopeful story and ⓐgive some insight into the hard
work that I had to put in.
Look at this picture of Picasso’s The Old Guitarist
behind me. My grandfather was a classical guitarist,
and on my 13th birthday, he gave me this picture
and a new guitar. After he passed away, I hung it
up in my room as a reminder of his love for music.
I wasn’t a musical genius, but I was better than
most. I was popular at school festivals, and I
thought I was born to be a musician. But things
were far from easy. In college, I had to compete
with classmates who were definitely more capable
than I was. I don’t even remember how many
contests I went to and came up short. I kept failing
ⓑno matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every
disappointment made me lose hope more and
more. I wanted to give up.
The funny thing was ⓒwhenever anyone asked me
to play a song for them, I would be so happy.
Although my dream was to record an album, the
reality was I probably wouldn’t make it. Then one
day, I looked at the picture of The Old Guitarist on
my
wall.
I
suddenly
remembered
what
my
grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a tiny
fraction of the thousands of artworks he created
during his lifetime are recognized by the public.
Then I thought of my grandfather and how he
loved playing, ⓓpracticing his art his entire life,
even without fame. I realized the only way to
become an old guitarist like him was ⓔto keep
playing.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ를 아래와 같이 전환할 때, 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: give → to give
ⓑ: no matter how hard → however hard
ⓒ: whenever → every time
ⓓ: practicing → to practice
ⓔ: to keep → keeping
solution: ⓓ 앞의 완전한 절(he loved playing)에 콤마(,)로 연결된 ‘practicing his art his entire life’는 흐름상 부대상황(~하면서) 을 나타내는 분사구문이므로, 현재분사 practicing을 to부정사 인 to practice로는 바꿀 수 없다. 참고로, 분사구문은 흐름상 적절한 접속사를 사용해 ‘접속사+주어+동사~’의 부사절로 바 꾸어 쓸 수 있으므로 while/as he practiced[was practicing]와 같이 전환할 수 있다.

The second point I want to make today ⓐto be
about thinking that your personality is fixed. Many
people believe that their personality falls into a
specific
category
and
often
ⓑblaming
their
weaknesses or failures on their personality type. For
example, they may say ⓒwhat they can’t do
something because they aren’t that kind of person.
However, personality categorizations are neither
absolute nor permanent.
Try to remember ourselves from ten years ago.
Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope
to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
If you choose ⓓbehaving differently and make

The second point I want to make today is about
thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people
believe that their personality falls into a specific
category and often blame their weaknesses or
failures on their personality type. For example, they
may say they can’t do something because they
aren’t that kind of person. However, personality
categorizations are ____________________________________.

from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
If you choose to behave differently and make
needed changes, your personality will also change.

only because they choose to be, so don’t limit
yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person
you want to become today.

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? In fact, most
people believe they make a worse impression than
they actually do. Researchers performed an experiment
where students were paired up for five-minute ice
breaking conversations. They were then asked to rate
how much they liked their partners. Additionally,
researchers asked participants if they thought their
partners liked them. Most participants’ estimations
of their partners’ responses were pessimistic, which
were opposite to the real responses. It turns out
that participants (A)___________________________________.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
In other words, our fixed attitudes may prevent us
from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry about
the impression you think you make on people;
chances
are
you
can
be
confident
that
the
impression you make is just fine.

do not care about whether their partners likethem or not

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym, playing
badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a hike.
However, those calories may also be burned by small,
seemingly unimportant activities we do throughout
the day, like standing up and sitting down, walking
around the house, washing dishes, doing the laundry,
taking out the garbage, and many others. These
actions are collectively called Non-Exercise Activity
Thermogenesis (NEAT) as they use up energy too!
For example, a 40-minute run will burn around 400
calories. (A)[Do / Doing] this could use up the excess
energy budget completely, but not everyone has 40
minutes a day to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps,
which (B)[is / are] like walking about 8 kilometers,
burns 400 calories as well. What this means is that
while a 40-minute run will burn 400 calories, doing
small things like more walking, taking stairs, or even
just (C)[clean / cleaning] your room can add up at
the end of the day, too.
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so
if you spend your day eating and not moving, your
body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While
NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with
the same benefits that exercise does, excess energy
still gets used up instead of being stored. You may
not necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy
balance, which is important for long term health.

body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While
NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with
the same benefits that exercise does, excess energy
still gets used up instead of being stored. You may
not necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy
balance, which is important for long term health.

through intense exercise but also through
daily movements such as doing housework or
walking around the house. (T/F)
(B) NEAT refers to small everyday activities that
consume energy even though they are not
formal exercise. (T/F)
(C) Only those who can spare 40 minutes for a
run can effectively deplete their daily excess
energy budget of 400 calories. (T/F)
(D) If a person eats but does not move much, the extra
energy may be stored in the body as fat. (T/F)
(E) Increasing NEAT gives the same benefits to the
heart and muscles as intense exercise does. (T/F)

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym, playing
badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a hike.
However, those calories may also be burned by small,
seemingly unimportant activities we do throughout
the day, like standing up and sitting down, walking
around the house, washing dishes, doing the laundry,
taking out the garbage, and many others. These
actions are collectively called Non-Exercise Activity
Thermogenesis (NEAT) as they use up energy too!
For example, a 40-minute run will burn around 400
calories. (A)[Do / Doing] this could use up the excess
energy budget completely, but not everyone has 40
minutes a day to go for a run. Taking 10,000 steps,
which (B)[is / are] like walking about 8 kilometers,
burns 400 calories as well. What this means is that
while a 40-minute run will burn 400 calories, doing
small things like more walking, taking stairs, or even
just (C)[clean / cleaning] your room can add up at
the end of the day, too.
Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so
if you spend your day eating and not moving, your
body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While
NEAT doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with
the same benefits that exercise does, excess energy
still gets used up instead of being stored. You may
not necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy
balance, which is important for long term health.

In the big picture, your body is like an energy
account book that ⓓneeds to be balanced. All the
food you eat is credit in the account, and you
need to spend energy to keep it all in balance.
Thus if you eat too much food without using the
excess energy, your body will store the extra as fat,
ⓔwhat is not healthy. Remember, standing uses
more energy than sitting, walking uses more energy
than standing, and running uses more energy than
walking, so let’s all keep moving, stay active, and
use our energy wisely for a healthier life!

body:
The answer to this requires a simple formula and
a little bit of math. The formula is an easy
equation: the total energy expenditure of the body
equals 「BMR + TEF + PA」. In the human body, the
energy from different foods people eat is used to
keep
everything
running
smoothly.
The
basal
metabolic rate (BMR) is a measurement of how
much energy is needed to stay alive; the thermic
effect of food (TEF) is a measurement of the energy
used to consume and absorb energy from food;
and physical activity (PA) is a measurement of the
energy _______________________________________. Learning
about the composition of these three elements can
help people make better choices for their health
and well-being.
Most of the energy the body uses each day is set
or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain working; this is called the basal metabolic
rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to
consume and absorb energy from food and is
called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for
the body to stay alive. The remaining 400 calories,
or 20%, is used for things people choose to do,
including various physical activities (PA) like working,
playing, and moving around. Maybe some of the
London public transportation workers spent the
remaining 20% differently, resulting in their different
health outcomes.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: used solely for high-intensity sports or structuredexercise
utilized in breaking down and absorbing foodnutrients
necessary to support vital functions while thebody is at rest
produced by the brain to regulate heartbeatand body functions
expended in physical activities beyond basiclife-sustaining needs
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

The second point I want to make today is about

believe that their personality falls into a specific

weaknesses or failures on their personality type. For

personality categorizations are neither absolute nor
(B)[permanent / permanently].

to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so (C)[do /
are] you. If you choose to behave differently and
make needed changes, your personality will also
change. People are predictable and consistent over
time only because they choose to be, so don’t limit
yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person
you want to become today.

(B)
(C)

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? In fact, most
people believe they make a (A)[better / worse]
impression
than
they
actually
do.
Researchers
performed an experiment where students were
paired up for five-minute ice breaking conversations.
They were then asked to rate how much they liked
their
partners.
Additionally,
researchers
asked
participants if they thought their partners liked
them.
Most
participants’
estimations
of
their
partners’ responses were (B)[optimistic / pessimistic],
which were opposite to the real responses. It turns
out that participants do not make bad impressions
but make better impressions than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often (C)[overestimate / underestimate]
ourselves based on our assumption of how others
might judge us. In other words, our fixed attitudes
may prevent us from reaching our true potential.
Don’t worry about the impression you think you
make on people; chances are you can be confident
that the impression you make is just fine.

(B) 뒤에 실제의 반응과는 정반대였으며, 참가자들은 나쁜 인 상을 주지 않고 그들이 생각하는 것보다 더 좋은 인상을 주는 것으로 드러났다는 내용이 이어지므로, 참가자들의 자신들의 파트너에 대한 평가는 비관적이었다는 흐름으로 pessimistic(비 관적인)이 적절하다. (C) 뒤에 In other words(다시 말해)로 연결되는 문장에서 우 리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있다고 환언하고 있으므로, 우리 자신이 나쁜 인상을 준다고 생각하는 우리의 고정된 태도로서, 우리가 흔히 다른 사람들이 우리를 어떻게 판단할지에 대한 추정에 근거해 우리 자신을 과소평가한다는 흐름으로 underestimate(~을 과소평가 하다)가 적절하다.

London Transport Workers Study
In the busy London streets of 1953, a special
study was conducted. Scientists observed more than
31,000 people ⓐwhich had various jobs on buses
and trains. Some jobs demanded lots of moving
around, like ticket collectors, while others, like
drivers, didn’t require much movement. What was
interesting ⓑwere that the workers with more active
jobs had fewer heart problems than those who sat
a lot. This implied that jobs requiring more moving
around were healthier for workers than those jobs
that ⓒwasn’t. That could account for the difference
in their health outcomes?
Most of the energy the body ⓓis used each day
is set or fixed. Assuming an energy input of 2,000
calories, about 1,400 calories, or 70%, goes to
essential functions such as keeping the heart and
the brain working; this is called the basal metabolic
rate (BMR). Around 200 calories, or 10%, is used to
consume and absorb energy from food and is
called the thermic effect of food (TEF). In short,
(A)BMR과 TEF는 신체가 생명을 유지하는 데 필요한
최소한의 에너지이다. The remaining 400 calories, or
20%, is used for things people choose to do,
including various physical activities (PA) like working,
playing, and ⓔmove around. Maybe some of the
London public transportation workers spent the
remaining 20% differently, resulting in their different
health outcomes.

Each gram of body fat contains about 9 calories, so if
you spend your day (A)[to eat / eating] and not moving,
your body may convert the 400 calories into 44 grams of
fat. This is not healthy over the long term. While NEAT
doesn’t provide the heart and muscles with the same
benefits (B)[what / that] exercise does, excess energy still
gets used up instead of being stored. You may not
necessarily get fit, but you’ll stay in energy balance,
(C)[which / that] is important for long term health.
Paying attention to NEAT has other health benefits
as well. Sitting too much can cause problems like
heart disease and muscle loss, so standing not only
increases NEAT but also decreases sitting time,
which is a win-win. As people get older, it may
become more difficult to stay healthy, so adopting a
lifestyle that maximizes NEAT is a good habit for
younger people to make. Walking more, taking
stairs, or even using smaller water cups so they
have to be refilled more often uses energy. Whether
it’s for weight management or trying to stay more
active during exam week, understanding NEAT is a
great way to maintain energy balance in the body.

stay active, and use our energy wisely for a
healthier life!

Then, what do people do with the remaining 400
calories? They may be burned by intense physical
exercise like jogging, working out at the gym,
playing badminton or tennis, or venturing out for a
hike. (A) However, those calories may also be
burned by small, seemingly unimportant activities
we do throughout the day, like standing up and
sitting down, walking around the house, washing
dishes, doing the laundry, taking out the garbage,
and many others. (B) For example, a 40-minute run
will burn around 400 calories. (C) Doing this could
use up the excess energy budget completely, but
not everyone has 40 minutes a day to go for a
run. (D) Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking
about 8 kilometers, burns 400 calories as well. (E)
What this means is that while a 40-minute run will
burn 400 calories, doing small things like more
walking, taking stairs, or even just cleaning your
room can add up at the end of the day, too.

Paying attention to NEAT has other health benefits
as well. Sitting too much can cause problems like
heart disease and muscle loss, so standing not only
increases NEAT but also decreases sitting time,
which is a win-win. As people get older, it may
become more difficult to stay healthy, so adopting
a lifestyle that maximizes NEAT is a good habit for
younger people to make. Walking more, taking
stairs, or even using smaller water cups so they
have to be refilled more often uses energy.
Whether it’s for weight management or trying to
stay more active during exam week, understanding
NEAT is a great way to maintain energy balance in
the body.

(B) ‘음식을 섭취하고 에너지를 흡수하는 데 사용되는’을 뜻하므로 to consume과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되 어야 한다. 따라서 to consume의 to를 생략한 동사원형 absorb가 적절하다. (C) 사역동사 help, 목적어 people에 이어지는 목적격보 어 자리이므로 동사원형 make가 적절하다. 5) The Equation for Total Energy Expenditure and Its Three Key Factors 제시문 신체의 총에너지 소비량을 위한 방정식과 그것의 세 가지 핵심 요소들 6) Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking about, burns 400 calories : • take 10,000 steps를 동명사로 변형하여 주어 Taking 10,000 steps를 작성한다. • ‘약 8킬로미터를 걷는 것과 같은 10,000보를 걷는 것’을 영작하기 위해 Taking 10,000 steps 뒤에 콤마(,)와 계속 적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 차례대로 쓰고, 선행사 Taking 10,000 steps는 단수이므로 which 뒤에 단수동사 is를 이어 쓴다. • ‘~와 같은’을 뜻하는 전치사 like와 전치사의 목적어로 동명사 walking을 쓴 뒤, 거리를 나타내는 8 kilometers 앞에 ‘약’의 의미를 갖는 about을 쓴다. • 주어 Taking 10,000 steps는 단수이므로 관계사절 뒤에 콤마(,)와 단수동사 burns를 쓰고 목적어 400 calories를 이어 쓴다. 7) ④: ⓓ required → requiring (명사절 접속사 that이 이끄는 절에서 동사 were가 뒤에 있으므로 주어 jobs를 수식하 는 분사 자리이며, jobs가 더 많은 움직임을 ‘필요로 하 영어1 비상(홍민표) S.U1 예상문제 2회 - 주관식(서답형) 2. BMR and TEF are the minimum energy required for the body to stay alive 5. The Equation for Total Energy Expenditure and Its Three Key Factors 6. Taking 10,000 steps, which is like walking about, burns 400 calories 는’ 주체이므로 required를 능동의 의미인 현재분사 requiring으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 주어 a special study가 ‘진행된’ 대상이므로 be동사 was와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 conducted는 적절하다. ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was interesting)을 이끌어 선행사 없이 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므 로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 What은 적절하다. ⓒ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(sat a lot)을 이끌어 workers를 가리키는 선행사 those를 수식하는 관계사절 을 이루고 있으므로, 선행사가 사람일 때 쓰는 주격 관 계대명사 who는 적절하다. ⓔ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(didn't)을 이끌어 선행사 those jobs를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주 격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다. 참고로 didn't은 didn't require moving around를 의미한다. 8) ④: (A) 뒤에서 활동량이 많은 직업과 적은 직업을 비교하고 있으므로 흐름상 ‘다양한’ 직업들이 자연스럽다. 따라서 various(다양한)가 적절하다. same 동일한 (B) 뒤에서 더 많이 움직이는 직업이 그렇지 않은 직업 보다 근로자의 건강에 더 좋다는 것을 암시했다고 했으 므로 흐름상 활동량이 많은 노동자들이 심장 질환이 ‘더 적었다’는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘fewer(더 적은)’가 적 절하다. more 더 많은 (C) 더 많이 움직이는 직업이 그렇지 않은 직업보다 근 로자의 건강에 더 좋다고 했으므로 그들의 건강 결과에 ‘차이’가 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 difference(차 이)가 적절하다. similarity 유사점 9) ②: (A) 동사 spend는 ‘spend+목적어+~ing(~하는 데 …를 보내다)’의 구조를 취해야 하며, 등위접속사 and 뒤에 not moving과도 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로 목적어 your day 뒤에 eating이 이어지는 것이 적절하다. (B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(exercise does)을 이끌어 선행사 the same benefits를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루 어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ health)을 이끌어 앞 절 전체를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다. 10) ⑤: 일상에서 걷기, 서 있기, 계단 이용하기와 같은 작은 움 직임(NEAT)을 늘리면 과잉 에너지가 지방으로 저장되 는 것을 막아 에너지 균형을 유지할 수 있으며, 이는 장기적으로 체중 관리와 장기적으로 전반적인 건강 유 지에 중요한 역할을 한다는 것의 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘에너지 균형과 건강을 유 지하도록 돕는 NEAT‘이다. 오답 ① 신체적 요구 측면에서 일상의 가벼운 활동과 고강도 운동의 동등함 ② NEAT가 근력 강화와 심장 건강에 미치는 긍정적인 영향 ③ 섭취량보다 에너지 소비를 극대화함으로써 체중을 줄이기 위한 간단한 공식 ④ 젊은 사람들이 NEAT를 통해 운동 수행 능력을 성취 하기 위한 전략들 11) ③: (A) 뒤에서 심장과 뇌를 작동시키는 것과 같은 기능들 이라고 했으므로 ‘필수적인’ 기능들이라는 흐름이 자연 스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 fundamental(근본적인), essential(필수적인), vital(생명 유지에 필수적인)이다. (B) 뒤에서 일, 놀이, 이동과 같은 다양한 신체 활동들 이 언급됐으므로 사람들이 하기로 ‘선택한’ 활동들이라 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적 절한 것은 opt(선택하다), choose(선택하다), decide(결 정하다)이다. 오답 ① 근본적인 주저하다 ② 불필요한 선택하다 ④ 생명 유지에 필수적인 필요로 하다 ⑤ 부차적인 결정하다 12) ⑤: 런던 대중교통 근로자 중 일부가 남은 20%의 에너지를 다르게 소비하여 다른 건강 결과를 얻었을 것이라는 것만 추정했을 뿐, 구체적으로 어떤 질병과 관련이 있 는지는 언급되지 않았으므로 ⑤ ‘런던 대중교통 근로자 들의 서로 다른 건강 결과와 관련된 특정 질병들은 무 엇인가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 인간 신체의 총에너지 소비량을 계산하는 데 사용 되는 수학적 공식은 무엇인가? (→신체의 총에너지 소 비량 = BMR+TEF+PA) ② 어떤 요소들이 인간 신체가 생명을 유지하기 위해 필요한 최소한의 에너지를 구성하는가? (→기초 대사율 (BMR)과 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)) ③ 음식을 섭취하고 영양분을 흡수하는 과정 동안 소 비되는 에너지를 가리키는 용어는 무엇인가? (→식이성 발열 효과(TEF)) ④ 하루 섭취량을 2,000칼로리로 가정할 때, 얼마나 많 은 에너지가 식이성 발열 효과(TEF)에 구체적으로 할당 되는가? (→약 200칼로리) 13) ①: 우리의 신체를 균형을 유지해야 하는 에너지 장부책으 로 비유하여, 음식을 섭취하면 균형을 유지하기 위해 에너지를 소비해야 한다고 했으므로 과잉 에너지를 사 용하지 않고 너무 많은 음식을 섭취하면 살이 찌고, 이 는 건강에 좋지 않다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈 칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ① ‘남는 에너지를 체지 방으로 저장하다’이다. 오답 ② 모든 영양소를 신체적인 힘(체력)으로 전환하다 ③ 자동으로 총칼로리 섭취량을 줄이다 ④ 여러 장기를 통해 남은 칼로리를 방출하다 ⑤ 장부 균형을 유지하기 위해 더 많은 음식을 요구하다 14) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 행동 또한 에너지를 소모하기 때문에 비운동성 활동 열 생성(NEAT)이라고 통칭한다.’ 라는 의미이다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 ‘These actions‘로 지칭될 운동이 아닌 일상적인 활동들이 먼저 제시되어 야 한다. 따라서 ‘일어서고 앉기, 집 안에서 돌아다니 기, 설거지하기, 빨래하기, 쓰레기 내다 버리기 등’과 같은 운동이 아닌 일상적인 활동들이 구체적으로 제시 되어 있는 문장 뒤이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 내용(에 너지 소모)에 대한 구체적인 수치로 강렬한 운동 못지 않게 NEAT가 에너지를 소비한다는 예를 들고 있는 문 장 앞인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다. 15) ⑤: 앞에서 우리가 하루 종일 하는 작고 사소해 보이는 활 동에 의해서도 칼로리가 소모되며 40분 달리기와 마찬 가지로 더 많이 걷거나 계단을 이용하거나 방을 청소 하는 등의 작은 활동도 하루가 끝날 때 합산될 수 있 다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘사소한 집안일들은 너무 미미해서 하루가 끝날 때 사용되는 총 에너지 양에 기여하지 못 한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 오답 ① 심지어 우리가 단순히 서 있거나 앉아 있을 때에도, 신체는 에너지를 필요로 한다. ② NEAT는 체계적인 운동보다는 사소한 일상적 움직임 을 통해 소모되는 에너지를 일컫는다. ③ 약 10,000보를 걷는 것은 총 칼로리 소모 측면에서 40분간의 달리기와 대략적으로 맞먹는다. ④ 신체적 제약이나 일정은 모든 사람들이 매일 40분 의 조깅에 전념하는 것을 막을 수 있다. 16) ⑤: (E) saves(절약하다) → uses(사용하다) 17) ⑤: ‘그렇다면 사람들은 남은 400칼로리를 어떻게 사용할까? ‘라는 주어진 글 뒤에 the remaining 400 calories를 They로 이어받아 질문에 대한 답변으로 격렬한 신체 운동과 작고 사소한 활동들에 의해 남은 칼로리가 소모 될 수 있다고 설명하는 (C), (C)의 마지막 문장에서 언 급된 작고 사소한 활동들을 These actions(이러한 행동 들)로 이어받아 이러한 행동들이 비운동성 활동 열 생 성(NEAT)이라고 불린다고 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막 문장에서는 NEAT 역시 에너지를 소모한다는 점을 강조 하기 위해 For example(예를 들어)을 사용하여 ‘40분 달리기는 400칼로리를 소모한다’라는 구체적인 수치를 제시한 뒤, ‘40분 달리기’를 Doing this로 이어받아 그 러한 운동이 남은 에너지를 모두 소모할 수 있음을 설 명하고, 이어서 10,000보 걷기 역시 같은 양의 칼로리 를 소모할 수 있다는 추가 예시를 제시하는 (A)로 이어 지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 18) ⑤: NEAT를 늘리는 생활 습관은 단순히 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이는 것뿐만 아니라, 걷기, 계단 오르기, 작은 활동들 처럼 일상 속 움직임을 통해 추가 에너지를 소모하게 해 주며, 이를 통해 건강 유지, 체중 관리, 에너지 균형 유지 등 다양한 장기적인 건강상의 이점을 제공한다고 했으므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘NEAT에 주 의를 기울이는 것이 필요한 이유’이다. 오답 ① 체계적인 운동이 건강을 개선시키는 데 있어서 일 상의 생활 방식 변화보다 더 나은 성과를 내는 이유 ② 신체 건강에 미치는 사소한 신체 활동들의 미미한 영향 ③ 자신의 활동 수준에 기반한 에너지 균형을 달성하는 방법 ④ 장수를 위해 좌식 습관을 없애야 할 필요성

Hello, my name is Laura Thompson, and I’m a
guidance counselor at the local college. I also have
a social media channel where I give advice to
young students like you. Today I’d like to talk to
you about two things that I hope will inspire you.
Let me start by asking you a question. Have you
ever asked yourself whether you made a good
impression on someone you just met? (A)___________,
most people believe they make a worse impression
than they actually do. Researchers performed an
experiment where students were paired up for
five-minute ice breaking conversations. They were
then asked to rate how much they liked their
partners. (B)___________, researchers asked participants
if they thought their partners liked them. Most
participants’ estimations of their partners’ responses
were pessimistic, which were opposite to the real
responses. It turns out that participants do not
make bad impressions but make better impressions
than they think.
The researchers coined a new term, the “liking
gap,” for this difference in perception or the
mismatch between how we perceive ourselves and
what others actually think of us. How is this helpful
for you? We often underestimate ourselves based
on our assumption of how others might judge us.
(C)___________, our fixed attitudes may prevent us
from reaching our true potential. Don’t worry about
the impression you think you make on people;
chances
are
you
can
be
confident
that
the
impression you make is just fine.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: In factHoweverIn contrast
In factAdditionallyIn other words
For exampleLikewiseIn contrast
ActuallyHoweverIn conclusion
For exampleAdditionallyIn other words
solution: (A) 방금 만난 사람에게 좋은 인상을 주었는지 스스로에게 물 어본 적이 있는가에 관한 질문에 대해 대부분의 사람들은 자 신이 실제로 주는 것보다 더 나쁜 인상을 준다고 믿는다는 사 실을 제시하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 예상과 다르거나 놀랄만한 사실을 덧붙일 때 사용하는 In fact(사실은)나 actually(실제로 는, 사실은)가 적절하다. (B) 실험 참가자들은 자신들의 파트너가 얼마나 마음에 들었는 지 평가하도록 요청받았다는 내용 뒤에 파트너가 자신을 좋아 한다고 생각하는지 물었다는 추가적인 요청에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 Additionally(추가로, 게다가)가 적절하다. (C) 우리는 흔히 다른 사람이 우리를 어떻게 판단할지에 대한 추정에 근거하여 우리 자신을 과소평가한다는 앞의 내용에 대 해, 우리의 고정된 태도는 우리가 진정한 잠재력에 도달하는 것을 막을 수 있다는 말로 바꿔 앞 내용의 요점을 다시 짚어 말하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 In other words(바꿔 말하면, 즉)가 적절하다.

body:
The second point I want to make today is about
thinking that your personality is fixed. Many people
believe that their personality falls into a specific
category and often blame their weaknesses or
failures on their personality type. For example, they
may say they can’t do something because they
aren’t that kind of person. However, personality
categorizations are neither absolute nor permanent.
Try to remember yourself from ten years ago.
Who was your favorite singer? What did you hope
to become when you grow up? Do you feel the
same way now? What will your answers be 10 years
from now? I bet you don’t know. Just like your
likes and future dreams keep changing, so do you.
If you (A)_______________________________________________
____________________, your personality will also change.
People are predictable and consistent over time
only because they choose to be, so don’t limit
yourself to a certain type. Start crafting the person
you want to become today.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: focus on past failures rather than future goals
avoid challenges that conflict with your personality
assume your future self will be the same as youare now
choose to behave differently and make neededchanges
try to find hobbies and jobs that suit yournatural personality
solution: 많은 사람들이 자신의 성격이 고정되어 있다고 잘못 생각하지 만 성격 분류는 절대적이지도 영구적이지도 않으며, 사람은 오 직 자신이 그렇게 하기로 선택했기 때문에 시간이 지나도 예 측 가능하고 변하지 않는 것이므로 특정 유형으로 자신을 제 한하지 말고 오늘부터 자신이 되고 싶은 사람을 만들기를 시 작하라고 했으므로, 변화를 만들기 위해 노력할 때 원하는 방 향으로 성격이 바뀔 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈 칸에는 ❹ ‘다른 방식으로 행동하고 필요한 변화를 만들기로 선택한다’가 적절하다.

body:
The funny thing was whenever anyone asked me
to play a song for them, I would be so happy.
Although my dream was to record an album, the
reality was I probably wouldn’t (A)[succeed / fail].
Then one day, I looked at the picture of The Old
Guitarist on my wall. I suddenly remembered what
my grandfather had told me about Picasso: only a
tiny fraction of the thousands of artworks he
created during his lifetime are recognized by the
public. Then I thought of my grandfather and how
he loved playing, practicing his art his entire life,
even without fame. I realized the only way to
become an old guitarist like him was to keep
playing.
The happy ending to this story is that after having
sent my recordings to countless producers, I finally
found one who was eager to work with me. One
thing led to another, and I finally (B)[signed / gave
up] a record deal. Opportunities only come to
those
who are
prepared. I
had
spent
years
performing on (C)[famous / unknown] streets and
writing songs no one recognized. The difficulties I
faced were part of my journey. If you love
something, keep trying. Someday an opportunity
may come knocking at your door, and you have to
be ready to welcome it.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: succeedsignedfamous
failgave upfamous
succeedsignedunknown
failsignedunknown
succeedgave upfamous
solution: (A) 음반을 녹음하는 것이 꿈이었지만 현실은 아마 성공하지 못할 것 같았다는 대조적인 흐름으로 wouldn’t 뒤에 succeed (성공하다)가 적절하다. (B) 마침내 자신과 함께 작업하기를 몹시 원하는 프로듀서를 찾았고, 하나의 일이 다른 일로 이어졌다는 내용 뒤에 마침내 음반 계약을 체결했다는 최종적인 결과가 이어지는 흐름으로, signed(서명했다)가 적절하다. (C) 자신에게 마침내 기회가 오기까지 겪었던 어려움들을 언급 하는 맥락이므로, 무명의 거리에서 공연하고 아무도 알아주지 않는 곡을 쓰며 여러 해를 보냈다는 흐름으로 unknown(알려 지지 않은)이 적절하다.

다음 글에 드러난 ‘I’의 심경 변화로 알맞은 것은?

I wasn’t a musical genius, but I was better than
most. I was popular at school festivals, and I
thought I was born to be a musician. But things
were far from easy. In college, I had to compete
with classmates who were definitely more capable
than I was. I don’t even remember how many
contests I went to and came up short. I kept failing
no matter how hard I tried. It seemed like every
disappointment made me lose hope more and
more. I wanted to give up.
choices: anxious → relieved

confident → frustrated
pessimistic → optimistic

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

During New York Fashion Week 2018, a woman
with a brightly decorated prosthetic leg proudly
walked the runway at a major fashion show. She
was Mama Cax, a model and influencer.
Cax was diagnosed with cancer at age 14 and lost
her right leg at 16 after surgery. At first, Cax was
depressed and struggled to accept her new body.
However, with the support of her family and
friends, Cax learned to love it. One day when she
was 26, Cax posted a picture on social media
showing her leg. “I didn’t think it could help
anyone,” she said in an interview, “But after receiving
messages of support, I realized my story could
inspire others.” After receiving support from others,
she began to use social media to share more about
her life and to inspire others. She proudly posted
pictures of herself wearing stylish prosthetic covers
and spoke out about body positivity and fashion. In
2016,
she
became
the
first
model
for
the
#RunwayForAll campaign. In 2018, she appeared on
the cover of major fashion magazines.
When asked, “How did you come to embrace
yourself?” she replied, “The truth is, like many
people, I’m still on my journey to self-love. There
are many barriers ahead.” In addition to modeling,
Cax showed her ability to overcome physical
barriers
by
swimming,
playing
basketball,
and
mountain climbing. She even finished the New York
City Marathon in a wheelchair.
Sadly, Mama Cax’s journey was cut short in 2019.
Although she is no longer with us, her journey will
remain in our hearts, inspiring us to overcome
limitations and find our own paths to success and
happiness.

solution: 암으로 인한 수술 후 오른쪽 다리를 잃었지만 자신의 새로운 몸을 받아들이고 사랑하는 방법을 배운 후, 자신의 삶을 소셜 미디어를 통해 공유하며 많은 사람들에게 신체에 대한 긍정에 대해 목소리를 내고 장애를 극복하는 능력을 보여주며 자기애 를 향한 여정을 계속했던 Mama Cax에 대한 이야기로, 그녀의 여정이 끝난 뒤에도 많은 사람들에게 한계를 극복하고 성공과 행복을 향한 자신만의 길을 찾도록 영감을 준다는 내용이므로, 글의 제목으로 ❸ ‘장애를 극복하고 자신을 받아들이는 것에 대한 Mama Cax의 영감을 주는 여정’이 적절하다.
